definition_zh: n. 转移；转向；改道；绕行路；消遣；分散注意力的举动
definition_en: the act of turning something aside from its course, a temporary detour, or an activity that entertains

senses.title: Turning aside
senses.definition: the act of changing the direction, course or use of something
senses.definitionCN: （名词）指改变某物的方向、路线或用途
senses.example: The diversion of the river took two years.
senses.exampleCN: 河流改道花了两年。
senses.why: A river pushed out of its old bed into a new channel.
senses.whyCN: 一条被推出旧河床、进入新河道的水流。

senses.title: A temporary detour
senses.definition: a route used for a short time while the main road is closed
senses.definitionCN: （名词）主路封闭时临时使用的路线
senses.example: Follow the diversion past the bridge works.
senses.exampleCN: 沿着绕行路经过桥梁施工段。
senses.why: Orange arrows pointing traffic onto a narrow lane.
senses.whyCN: 橙色箭头把车流指向一条窄巷。

senses.title: Pleasant entertainment
senses.definition: an activity that gives amusement or relaxation

senses.example: The hotel offers evening diversions for guests.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店为客人提供晚间消遣。
senses.why: A deck of cards and a chess board on a rainy afternoon.
senses.whyCN: 雨天午后的一副纸牌和一张棋盘。

senses.title: A distracting move
senses.definition: something done to draw attention away from what matters
senses.definitionCN: （名词）为把注意力从要紧事上引开而做的举动
senses.example: He created a diversion so the others could slip out.
senses.exampleCN: 他制造了一个幌子，好让其他人溜出去。
senses.why: A firecracker popping at the far end of the yard.
senses.whyCN: 院子另一头炸响的一枚爆竹。

senses.title: Redirected resources
senses.definition: the act of moving money or supplies to a different purpose
senses.definitionCN: （名词）把资金或物资转作别的用途
senses.example: The diversion of funds was reported to the board.
senses.exampleCN: 资金挪用一事已上报董事会。
senses.why: A pipe carrying water from one tank into another.
senses.whyCN: 一根把水从一只水箱引到另一只的管子。

intro.en: Diversion comes from Latin divertere, to turn aside, built from di- plus vertere, to turn; the noun suffix -ion turns the action into a thing you can name.
intro.cn: diversion 来自拉丁语 divertere「转到一边」，由 di- 加 vertere「转」组成；名词后缀 -ion 把这个动作变成一件可以指称的事。

items.en: Latin vertere means to turn.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vertere 意为转。

items.en: Divertere means to turn aside or away.
items.cn: divertere 意为转到一边或转开。

items.en: The related noun versio means a turning.
items.cn: 相关名词 versio 意为一次转动。

items.en: Old French diversion carries the sense of turning away.
items.cn: 古法语 diversion 带有转开的意思。

items.en: The word comes to mean a temporary route around road works.
items.cn: 这个词转而指绕过道路施工的临时路线。

items.en: Diversion also names entertainment and a distracting move.
items.cn: diversion 也指消遣与分散注意力的举动。

note.en: Diversion is a turning aside; its look-alikes share the turn root, and its neighbours name the route, the pulled attention and the fun.
note.cn: diversion 是一次转开；形近词共用「转」的词根，近义词则分别指那条路、被拉开的注意力和那份乐趣。

definition_zh: 创业者；企业家；承担风险创办事业的人
definition_en: a person who starts a business and takes on the financial risk in order to make a profit
core_image: 一个人把全部积蓄换成一台机器，机器的开关还没按下
scene: 那位年轻创业者把全部积蓄投进一台新烘干机，开了一家自助洗衣店。 The young entrepreneur put her entire savings into a new drying machine and opened a self-service laundry.
sceneCN: 那位年轻创业者把全部积蓄投进一台新烘干机，开了一家自助洗衣店；句中的 entrepreneur 指「自己出资创办事业并承担风险的人」（第 1 个义项：创办新事业的人）。图中可辨识物件：烘干机、投币盒、洗衣篮、租约。

pos.zh: 创业者；企业家；承办人

forms.label: 相关名词（创业活动、创业精神）

senses.title: Someone who starts a venture
senses.definition: a person who sets up a new business, usually committing their own money and effort
senses.definitionCN: 创办新企业的人，通常投入自己的钱与精力
senses.example: The young entrepreneur put her entire savings into a new drying machine and opened a self-service laundry.
senses.exampleCN: 那位年轻创业者把全部积蓄投进一台新烘干机，开了一家自助洗衣店。
senses.why: The French source means 'one who undertakes', so the word names the person who takes a venture in hand.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「承担者」，因此这个词指把事业接到手里的人。

senses.title: An organizer of the factors of production
senses.titleCN: 组织生产要素的企业家
senses.definition: in economics, the person who combines capital, labour and materials into a working business
senses.definitionCN: 经济学上把资本、劳动与原料组合成可运转企业的人
senses.example: The textbook defines the entrepreneur as the one who coordinates land, labour and capital.
senses.exampleCN: 教科书把企业家定义为协调土地、劳动与资本的人。
senses.why: Classical economics needed a name for the agent who assembles the other inputs, and borrowed this French word for it.
senses.whyCN: 古典经济学需要为「把其他要素组合起来的人」起个名字，就借用了这个法语词。

senses.title: A self-employed owner-operator
senses.definition: a person who runs their own small business and earns from it rather than from a wage
senses.definitionCN: 经营自己的小企业、靠经营所得而非工资生活的人
senses.example: Many entrepreneurs in the town run one-person workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上许多创业者经营只有一个人的作坊。
senses.why: Owning the venture and working in it are one act for a small operator, so the word covers the self-employed.
senses.whyCN: 对小经营者来说，拥有事业与在其中劳作是同一件事，因此这个词涵盖自雇者。

senses.title: The bearer of business risk
senses.definition: the party who risks their own capital on an uncertain outcome and keeps the residual gain or loss
senses.definitionCN: 把自有资本押在不确定结果上、并承担剩余盈亏的一方
senses.example: The entrepreneur bears the loss if the shop fails.
senses.exampleCN: 如果店铺失败，损失由创业者承担。
senses.why: Undertaking includes taking the downside, so risk bearing became the defining economic mark of the word.
senses.whyCN: 「承担」本来就包含承担坏结果，因此负险成了这个词在经济上的标志。

senses.title: An innovator who breaks old routines
senses.definition: a person who introduces a new product, method or market and displaces established ways of doing things
senses.definitionCN: 引入新产品、新方法或新市场，取代既有做法的人
senses.example: Schumpeter treated the entrepreneur as the force that destroyed old combinations.
senses.exampleCN: 熊彼特把企业家看作摧毁旧组合的力量。
senses.why: Innovation is a form of undertaking: the new combination has to be carried through against existing habits.
senses.whyCN: 创新是承担的一种形态：新的组合必须顶着既有习惯被推行到底。

senses.title: A contractor or promoter of a project
senses.definition: a person who takes on and organizes a specific project, such as a public work or an entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 承接并组织某个具体项目的人，如公共工程或演出
senses.example: The entrepreneur behind the festival booked the whole square.
senses.exampleCN: 操办这个节庆的承办人把整个广场都订下了。
senses.why: The word entered English for the promoter of a musical or theatrical production, and this project sense survives.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初进入英语时指音乐或戏剧演出的承办人，这一项目义保留至今。

senses.title: A repeat founder
senses.definition: a person who starts one venture after another, often selling each before beginning the next
senses.definitionCN: 接连创办事业、常在开始下一个之前卖掉前一个的人
senses.example: The serial entrepreneur had sold three companies by forty.
senses.exampleCN: 这位连续创业者到四十岁时已经卖掉了三家公司。
senses.why: If starting is the core act, repeating it becomes a recognisable type of person.
senses.whyCN: 如果创办是核心动作，反复做这个动作就成为一种可辨认的人。

senses.title: A calculated gambler in business
senses.titleCN: 敢于下注的商界冒险者
senses.definition: a person who commits heavily to an uncertain commercial bet, admired or blamed for boldness
senses.definitionCN: 把大量资源押在不确定的商业赌注上、因大胆而被赞赏或指责的人
senses.example: The entrepreneur staked the factory on a single export contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这位冒险者把整座工厂押在一份出口合同上。
senses.why: Risk bearing pushed to its extreme looks like gambling, and the word takes on that colour in everyday speech.
senses.whyCN: 把负险推到极端就像赌博，这个词在日常说法里就带上了这层色彩。

intro.en: Entrepreneur is French for 'one who undertakes', from entreprendre 'to take in hand'. English borrowed it in the eighteenth century for a promoter of entertainments, and economics gave it its modern sense in the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: entrepreneur 是法语「承担者」，出自 entreprendre「着手、承担」。英语在十八世纪借入，指演出承办人；经济学在十九世纪赋予它现代含义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Entreprendre 'to undertake' joined a prefix meaning 'between' with prendre 'to take', itself from Latin prehendere 'to grasp'.
items.cn: entreprendre「承担」把意为「之间」的前缀与 prendre「拿取」结合，后者出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」。

items.en: Entrepreneur named the person who undertakes a task, with no necessary link to trade or profit.
items.cn: entrepreneur 指承担某项任务的人，与买卖或利润没有必然联系。

items.en: English used entrepreneur first for someone who organized public entertainments, especially musical or theatrical productions.
items.cn: 英语最初用 entrepreneur 指组织公共演出的人，尤其是音乐或戏剧制作。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economists, notably Jean-Baptiste Say, made the word mean the agent who combines production and bears the risk.
items.cn: 十九世纪的经济学家，尤其是萨伊，使这个词指组合生产并承担风险的主体。

items.en: Schumpeter shifted the emphasis from mere ownership to innovation, and that reading dominates business writing today.
items.cn: 熊彼特把重点从单纯的所有权转到创新，这一读法如今主导商业写作。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same taking root; group two holds names for people who run or start businesses.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「拿取」词根的词；第二组是经营或创办企业者的称呼。

entries.definition: The undertaking itself, whether a firm or a project; entrepreneur is the person who carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 指被承担的事业本身，无论企业或项目；entrepreneur 是承担它的人。

entries.definition: An adjective describing the outlook or style of such a person, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述这类人的眼光或风格，不指人本身。

entries.definition: The activity or skill of starting ventures; the noun names the practice, not the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 指创办事业的活动或本领；命名的是实践，不是实践者。

entries.definition: A person who acts like a founder inside an existing company; the prefix marks the setting.
entries.definitionCN: 指在现有公司内部像创办者那样行事的人；前缀标明了场景。

entries.definition: A person who establishes an organization; it records the act of setting up, not the ongoing risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指建立某个组织的人；记录的是创立动作，不是持续承担的风险。

entries.definition: A man engaged in trade; it does not require that he started the firm or bears its risk.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事买卖的男子；不要求他创办企业或承担其风险。

entries.definition: An owner or manager of large manufacturing enterprises; grander and narrower than entrepreneur.
entries.definitionCN: 指大型制造企业的所有者或管理者；比 entrepreneur 更宏大也更窄。

entries.definition: A promoter of concerts, theatre or opera; it keeps the older English sense of entrepreneur.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐会、戏剧或歌剧的承办人；保留了 entrepreneur 在英语中较旧的意义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: French for 'one who undertakes': the person who takes the venture in hand.
normal.cn: 法语意为「承担者」：把事业接到手里的人。

normal.en: The family runs entrepreneur, entrepreneurs, entrepreneurial and entrepreneurship.
normal.cn: 同族词有 entrepreneur、entrepreneurs、entrepreneurial 与 entrepreneurship。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the types: a young entrepreneur, a serial entrepreneur, a social entrepreneur.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：年轻创业者、连续创业者、社会创业者。

normal.en: The same root gives enterprise for the venture and entrepreneur for the person.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 enterprise（事业）与 entrepreneur（承担者）。

normal.en: Economics added the risk-bearing sense; innovation writing added the disruptive sense.
normal.cn: 经济学加上负险义，创新论述又加上颠覆义。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing on a heavy lever before anyone knows whether it will move.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握住一根重杠杆，还没人知道它会不会动。

abstract.en: Picture a savings jar emptied in one motion onto a workbench.
abstract.cn: 想象一只存钱罐被一次性倒空在作台上。

abstract.en: Picture a map with one route drawn and all the others left blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只画了一条路线、其余都空着的地图。

examples.en: The city offers cheap office space to young entrepreneurs.
examples.cn: 该市向年轻创业者提供廉价办公空间。

examples.en: An entrepreneur must accept that most attempts fail.
examples.cn: 创业者必须接受大多数尝试会失败。

examples.en: The entrepreneur sold the company and started a second one.
examples.cn: 这位创业者卖掉公司后又创办了第二家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把存钱罐倒空在作台上，旁边是一台新机器 → 创业者

root: 法语 entrepreneur「承担者」，出自 entreprendre「着手、承担」= entre-「之间」+ prendre「拿取」，后者出自拉丁 prehendere「抓住」；英语十八世纪借入，十九世纪由经济学固定为「承担风险创办事业的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person taking a venture in hand: the founder, the organizer of production, the self-employed operator, the risk bearer, the innovator, the project promoter, the repeat founder, and the bold gambler.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个把事业接到手里的人：创办者、生产组织者、自雇经营者、风险承担者、创新者、项目承办人、连续创业者，以及大胆下注的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person emptying a savings jar onto a workbench beside a new machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把存钱罐倒空在作台上，旁边是一台新机器。

branches.en: TAKING IT ON: founding a venture and running it alone are the same act at different sizes.
branches.cn: 接下事业：创办企业与独自经营，是同一动作的不同规模。

branches.en: ORGANIZER: economics turns the undertaker into the agent who assembles land, labour and capital.
branches.cn: 组织者：经济学把承担者变成组合土地、劳动与资本的主体。

branches.en: BET: bearing the downside and staking everything are the same risk at different temperatures.
branches.cn: 赌注：承担坏结果与押上全部，是同一风险的两种温度。

branches.en: INNOVATOR: the new combination must be carried through against old habits.
branches.cn: 创新者：新的组合必须顶着旧习惯被推行到底。

branches.en: REPEATED UNDERTAKING: a promoter of shows and a repeat founder both take project after project in hand.
branches.cn: 反复承担：演出承办人与连续创业者，都一件接一件地把项目接到手里。

intro.en: Entrepreneur is a French agent noun built from a taking verb; its English family supplies the adjective and the practice noun.
intro.cn: entrepreneur 是由「拿取」动词构成的法语施事名词；英语词族给出形容词与实践名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin prehendere gives prehensile and comprehend; French entreprendre gives entrepreneur, enterprise and enterprising.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prehendere 给出 prehensile 与 comprehend；法语 entreprendre 给出 entrepreneur、enterprise 与 enterprising。

items.example: The root pictures a hand closing on a tool.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根描绘一只手合拢抓住工具。

items.example: The verb means to take a task in hand.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词意为把任务接到手里。
这位创业者开了那家洗衣店。
十位创业者加入了这项计划。

definition_zh: 贸易逆差；贸易赤字；进口大于出口的差额
definition_en: the amount by which a country's imports of goods exceed its exports in a given period
core_image: 一架天平，进口一侧的砝码堆得更高，出口一侧翘起，秤杆上标出一个负数
scene: 经济部门的简报会上，分析员把全年进口额与出口额相减，得出一个需要向公众解释的负差额。 The report showed a trade deficit for the third year in a row.
sceneCN: 这里指「进口超过出口的差额」，对应第 1 个义项：一定时期内进口总值大于出口总值的部分；句意为报告显示该国连续第三年出现贸易逆差。画面要点：简报屏幕、两条柱状数据、天平、负号标记。

pos.zh: 贸易逆差；贸易赤字（可数，复数 trade deficits）

derivatives.zh: 赤字；缺额（trade deficit 的核心名词，指收支中短少的部分）
不足的；有缺陷的（同出拉丁 deficere「缺少」，语义偏向质量或数量不够）
缺乏；缺陷（deficient 加名词后缀，指不足的状态）
不足地（deficient 加副词后缀，指以不足的方式）
贸易；交易（短语的前半，源自古英语与低地德语中表示「路径、往来」的词）

senses.title: Imports exceeding exports
senses.definition: the amount by which the value of a country's imports exceeds the value of its exports in a period
senses.definitionCN: 一定时期内一国进口总值超过出口总值的部分
senses.example: The report showed a trade deficit for the third year in a row.
senses.exampleCN: 报告显示该国连续第三年出现贸易逆差。
senses.why: Latin deficit means 'it is lacking', so the phrase names a gap: more value enters as goods than leaves as goods.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 deficit 意为「它缺了」，因此这个短语指一道缺口：以货物形式进来的价值多于出去的价值。

senses.title: The size of the gap
senses.definition: the measured size of the shortfall, usually in money terms
senses.definitionCN: 这一短少部分的计量规模，通常以货币计
senses.example: The trade deficit reached forty billion dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易逆差达到四百亿美元。
senses.why: Deficit is countable, so the phrase can name a figure that rises, falls or sets a record.
senses.whyCN: deficit 可数，因此这个短语能指一个会上升、下降或创纪录的数字。

senses.title: A bilateral deficit with one partner
senses.titleCN: 与某一贸易伙伴的双边逆差
senses.definition: the excess of imports from one country over exports to that same country
senses.definitionCN: 从某一国进口超过向该国出口的部分
senses.example: The trade deficit with that partner dominated the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 与那个伙伴的贸易逆差主导了会谈。
senses.why: Trade is counted partner by partner, so the same gap can be attributed to a single relationship.
senses.whyCN: 贸易按伙伴逐一对计，因此同一道缺口可以归属于单一关系。

senses.title: The deficit in goods alone
senses.definition: the shortfall measured on goods only, leaving services aside
senses.definitionCN: 只按货物计算、把服务放在一边的差额
senses.example: The goods trade deficit is larger than the overall figure.
senses.exampleCN: 货物贸易逆差大于总体数字。
senses.why: Statistical systems separate goods from services, so the phrase is often qualified to show which ledger is meant.
senses.whyCN: 统计体系把货物与服务分开，因此这个短语常被限定，以说明看的是哪一本账。

senses.title: The deficit as a share of the economy
senses.titleCN: 以占经济总量的比例表示的逆差
senses.definition: the deficit expressed as a percentage of gross domestic product
senses.definitionCN: 以国内生产总值的百分比表示的逆差
senses.example: The trade deficit equals three percent of output.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易逆差相当于产出的百分之三。
senses.why: A raw number means little without scale, so economists divide it by the size of the economy.
senses.whyCN: 没有尺度，裸数字意义不大，因此经济学家用经济规模来除它。

senses.title: The deficit and its financing
senses.definition: the deficit viewed together with the capital inflows that fund it
senses.definitionCN: 与为其提供资金的资本流入一并看待的逆差
senses.example: A trade deficit must be matched by capital inflow.
senses.exampleCN: 贸易逆差必须由资本流入来对应。
senses.why: Goods flowing in are paid for by money or claims flowing out, so the gap always has a financial twin.
senses.whyCN: 货物流入要由资金或债权流出支付，因此这道缺口总有一个金融上的孪生面。

senses.title: The deficit as a political argument
senses.definition: the deficit used in debate as evidence of unfair trade or weak industry
senses.definitionCN: 在争论中被用作不公平贸易或产业疲弱之证据的逆差
senses.example: Politicians cite the trade deficit when arguing for tariffs.
senses.exampleCN: 政客主张加征关税时援引贸易逆差。
senses.why: A single number is easy to campaign with, so the phrase acquired a rhetorical life beyond accounting.
senses.whyCN: 一个数字便于竞选宣传，因此这个短语获得了超出会计范围的说服力。

senses.title: The deficit narrowing or widening
senses.titleCN: 逆差的收窄或扩大趋势
senses.definition: the direction in which the gap is moving over successive periods
senses.definitionCN: 这道缺口在连续各期中的变化方向
senses.example: A weaker currency helped narrow the trade deficit.
senses.exampleCN: 货币走弱帮助收窄了贸易逆差。
senses.why: Because the phrase names a flow over time, it is naturally described as widening, narrowing or reversing.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个短语指一段时间内的流量，自然会有扩大、收窄或反转等说法。

intro.en: Trade deficit joins trade, a word of path and exchange, with deficit, a Latin verb form meaning 'it is lacking'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: trade deficit 把表示「路径与往来」的 trade，与拉丁动词形式 deficit「它缺了」组合起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Trade probably came into English from Middle Low German or Dutch, where it meant a track or course, and English widened it to commerce and exchange.
items.cn: trade 很可能经中古低地德语或荷兰语进入英语，原指路径或行程，英语把它扩展到商业往来。

items.en: Deficere meant 'to fail, run short, be lacking', built on de- 'away' and facere 'to do or make'.
items.cn: deficere 意为「失败、短缺、缺少」，由 de-「离开」与 facere「做、造」构成。

items.en: Deficit is the third person singular present of deficere, 'it is lacking'; accountants took the verb form and used it as a noun.
items.cn: deficit 是 deficere 的第三人称单数现在时，意为「它缺了」；会计把这个动词形式借来当名词用。

items.en: English adopted deficit in the eighteenth century for a shortfall in accounts, especially public accounts.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪吸收 deficit，指账目中的短少，尤指公共账目。

items.en: As trade statistics became routine, the phrase trade deficit fixed the goods gap beside the older budget deficit.
items.cn: 随着贸易统计常规化，trade deficit 这一说法把货物缺口与较早的预算赤字区分开来。

note.en: The first group shares the lacking root or looks close to it; the second group names related gaps that are measured differently.
note.cn: 第一组共享「缺少」词根或与之外形相近；第二组是算法不同的相关缺口。

entries.definition: Any amount by which money falls short; alone it usually means a budget deficit, while trade deficit specifies the goods account.
entries.definitionCN: 任何资金短少的数额；单独使用时通常指预算赤字，而 trade deficit 特指货物账目。

entries.definition: Lacking something needed, often a nutrient or a quality; it describes a condition, not an account.
entries.definitionCN: 缺少所需之物，常指营养或品质；它描述状态，不描述账目。

entries.definition: A shortage or a flaw, such as a vitamin deficiency; it is not a trade measure.
entries.definitionCN: 短缺或缺陷，如维生素缺乏；它不是贸易指标。

entries.definition: Exports exceeding imports; the same ledger with the sign reversed.
entries.definitionCN: 出口超过进口；同一本账，符号相反。

entries.definition: An informal word for the same shortfall; it stresses the hole rather than the accounting term.
entries.definitionCN: 同一短少的非正式说法；它强调那个窟窿，而不是会计术语。

entries.definition: A shortfall covering goods, services and income flows; a trade deficit is only the goods part.
entries.definitionCN: 涵盖货物、服务与收入流的短少；贸易逆差只是其中的货物部分。

entries.definition: The gap between public spending and revenue; it concerns the state's purse, not the goods ledger.
entries.definitionCN: 公共支出与收入之间的缺口；它关乎国库，而非货物账目。

entries.definition: Any mismatch between two sides; it can describe trade without saying which side is larger.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧任何不匹配；它可以描述贸易，却不说哪一侧更大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb form, the real trade word and real statistical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词形式、真实的贸易词与真实统计搭配。

normal.en: Deficit is literally 'it is lacking', so a trade deficit is the ledger saying something is short.
normal.cn: deficit 字面是「它缺了」，因此贸易逆差就是账本在说短了一截。

normal.en: The opposite phrase is trade surplus, the same ledger with the other sign.
normal.cn: 反义说法是 trade surplus，同一本账的另一符号。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the uses: run a trade deficit, widen the deficit, a record deficit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示用法：出现逆差、扩大逆差、创纪录逆差。

normal.en: Deficit is countable, so it takes a, rises, falls and reaches a figure.
normal.cn: deficit 可数，因此能带冠词，能上升、下降、达到某个数字。

normal.en: Keep the three ledgers apart: goods, current account and government budget.
normal.cn: 要把三本账分开：货物账、经常账户账与政府预算账。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the import pan sinks and the export pan rises, and a minus sign hangs on the beam.

examples.cn: 自削减关税以来，该国一直处于贸易逆差。

examples.en: A falling currency can shrink the trade deficit over time.
examples.cn: 货币贬值可以逐渐缩小贸易逆差。

examples.en: The bilateral trade deficit with that partner hit a new high.
examples.cn: 与该伙伴的双边贸易逆差创下新高。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one gap: the excess of imports over exports, its size, its bilateral form, its goods-only measure, its share of output, its financing, its political use and its direction over time.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一道缺口：进口超过出口的部分、其数额、其双边形式、仅计货物的算法、其占产出的比例、其资金来源、其政治用途，以及其随时间的走向。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale with the import pan heavier and a minus sign on the beam.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架天平，进口那端更重，横梁上有个负号。

branches.en: BASE GAP: the ledger records more incoming than outgoing value.
branches.cn: 基础缺口：账上记的流入价值多于流出价值。

branches.en: MEASURE AND TREND: the gap has a size and a direction.
branches.cn: 数额与趋势：这道缺口有大小，也有走向。

branches.en: ONE PARTNER: the same gap can be attributed to a single relationship.
branches.cn: 单一伙伴：同一缺口可归属于一段双边关系。

branches.en: SCOPE AND SCALE: goods alone, or the gap as a share of output.
branches.cn: 范围与尺度：或只计货物，或折算为产出的比例。

branches.en: MONEY AND POLITICS: the gap is financed by inflows and argued over in public.
branches.cn: 金钱与政治：缺口由流入资金对应，也在公共争论中被援引。

intro.en: Trade deficit is a phrase of two free words, one about exchange and one a Latin verb form frozen as a noun.

latinIntro.en: Latin deficere 'to be lacking' gives deficit, deficient and deficiency; trade has a Germanic origin and gives trading, trader and trademark.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 deficere「缺少」衍生 deficit、deficient 与 deficiency；trade 源自日耳曼语，衍生 trading、trader 与 trademark。

sceneCN: 这里指一段时间内一次接一次、中间没有断开（第 1 个义项：时间上接连无间断）；句意为她连续三个赛季夺得冠军。图中可辨识物件：电子计时牌、选手名次、连成一列的赛季记录。

senses.title: Following in time without a break
senses.definition: happening in one period after another with nothing missing in between
senses.definitionCN: 一个时段接一个时段地发生，中间没有缺失
senses.example: The team trained for five consecutive days before the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛前，这支队伍连续训练了五天。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to follow closely, so the word begins with one thing pressing right behind another.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为紧跟，因此这个词最初就是一物紧贴另一物之后。

senses.title: Counting in an unbroken run
senses.definition: used of numbers or amounts that follow in an unbroken order
senses.definitionCN: 用于按不间断次序相随的数字或数量
senses.example: Write the consecutive numbers from one to ten.
senses.exampleCN: 写出一到十的连续数字。
senses.why: Counting is the plainest example of following on, with no value skipped between two terms.
senses.whyCN: 计数是「依次相随」最朴素的例子，两个数之间没有跳过的值。

senses.title: A run of wins
senses.definition: describing victories or successes that come one after another without a defeat between them
senses.definitionCN: 指一场接一场的胜利或成功，中间没有失败
senses.example: The club recorded four consecutive victories in the league.
senses.exampleCN: 这家俱乐部在联赛中取得四连胜。
senses.why: Sport counts streaks, and a streak is exactly a series with no gap in it.
senses.whyCN: 体育要数连续纪录，而连续纪录正是一个没有缺口的序列。

senses.title: Adjacent in a series
senses.definition: placed next to each other in an ordered set, as with numbers or seats
senses.definitionCN: 在有序集合中彼此相邻，如号码或座位
senses.example: The tickets bear consecutive serial numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这些票的编号是连号的。
senses.why: When items are numbered, following on means occupying the very next place.
senses.whyCN: 当物件被编号时，依次相随便意味着占据紧接着的那一位。

senses.title: A chain of linked events
senses.definition: describing events in which each one follows from the one before it
senses.definitionCN: 指每个事件都由前一个事件引出的情形
senses.example: The report describes a consecutive chain of failures.
senses.exampleCN: 报告描述了一连串前后相承的失误。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant to result from, so following in time can become following as a consequence.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词也意为「由……导致」，因此时间上的相随可以变成因果上的相承。

senses.title: The grammar of result
senses.definition: naming a clause that expresses the result of what the main clause states
senses.definitionCN: 指表达主句所述内容之结果的从句
senses.example: The grammar book explains how a consecutive clause expresses result.
senses.exampleCN: 这本语法书讲解结果从句如何表达结果。
senses.why: Grammarians borrowed the adjective for clauses where the second statement follows from the first.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家借这个形容词指第二个陈述由第一个陈述引出的从句。

senses.title: Unbroken shifts or operation
senses.definition: describing work periods that run one after another without a pause
senses.definitionCN: 指一个接一个运行、中间不停顿的工作时段
senses.example: The plant runs three consecutive shifts during the peak season.
senses.exampleCN: 生产旺季，工厂连续开三个班次。
senses.why: Industry measures time in shifts, and consecutive shifts leave no idle gap between them.
senses.whyCN: 工业以班次计量时间，而连续班次之间没有空闲的间隔。

senses.title: Year-after-year climate records
senses.definition: used of weather or climate data gathered over an unbroken series of years
senses.definitionCN: 用于在连续多年中收集的天气或气候数据
senses.example: Records show three consecutive dry years in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 记录显示该地区连续三年干旱。
senses.why: Climate science compares year to year, and a run of years with no break is the basic unit of a trend.
senses.whyCN: 气候科学逐年比较，而一段没有中断的年份正是趋势的基本单位。

intro.en: Consecutive comes from Latin consequi, to follow closely, from con-, together, and sequi, to follow; the past participle consecutus produced Late Latin consecutivus, which English borrowed in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「consequi」紧跟、随后，由「con-」一起与「sequi」跟随构成；过去分词「consecutus」产生晚期拉丁语「consecutivus」，英语在十七世纪借入。

items.en: To follow is the core of the word, and the same verb stands behind sequence and sequel.
items.cn: 跟随是这个词的核心，同一个动词也构成「sequence」与「sequel」的词源。

items.en: The prefix means together or along with, so following becomes following on.
items.cn: 这个前缀意为一起或随之，于是「跟随」变成「紧跟着」。

items.en: The verb meant to follow closely, to come after, and also to result from something.
items.cn: 这个动词意为紧跟、随后，也意为由某事物导致。

items.en: The past participle described what has followed, and it is the stem before the English ending.
items.cn: 这个过去分词描述已经跟随而来的事物，是英语词尾之前的词干。

items.en: The later adjective named things that follow in order or form a series.
items.cn: 这个晚期形容词指按次序相随或构成序列的事物。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century for things coming one after another.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个形容词，用于一个接一个到来的事物。

note.en: The first group looks like consecutive or shares its Latin stem; the second group names neighbouring ideas of things following in order. Note that successive stresses the order of items, from Latin sub- and cedere, to come after, while consecutive stresses that no gap separates them.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「consecutive」相近或共享拉丁词干；第二组是与「依次跟随」相邻的说法。要注意「successive」强调各项的次序，出自拉丁语「sub-」与「cedere」跟随在后；而「consecutive」强调中间没有间隔。

entries.definition: In an unbroken order, one after another.
entries.definitionCN: 指不间断地依次发生。

entries.definition: The state of following in sequence, a rare noun from the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 指依次相随的状态，是同一词干的罕见名词。

entries.definition: The quality of being unbroken in sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指序列不中断的性质。

entries.definition: A result that follows from an action; it shares the Latin verb but not the sense of sequence.
entries.definitionCN: 指由行为引出的结果；共享拉丁动词，但没有「连续」之义。

entries.definition: To set something apart as sacred; it looks close but belongs to a word for making sacred.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物定为神圣；形近但属于「使神圣」那一系。

entries.definition: Following in order, one after another, with emphasis on the sequence rather than on gaps.
entries.definitionCN: 指依次相随，强调次序，而不强调有无间隔。

entries.definition: Arranged in a fixed order, one step or item after another.
entries.definitionCN: 指按固定次序排列，一步或一项接一项。

entries.definition: Going on without any stop or break, often of time or movement.
entries.definitionCN: 指不停顿、不中断，常用于时间或运动。

entries.definition: Not broken off at any point, used of a stretch of time or activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指一段时间或活动在任何节点都未被打断。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the Latin follow verb behind the word, its real family and the everyday things counted in runs.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用这个词背后的拉丁语「跟随」动词、真实同族词，以及日常中成串计数的事物。

normal.en: The Latin sequi is to follow, and con- adds the sense of coming right along after.
normal.cn: 拉丁语「sequi」是跟随，「con-」加上「紧随其后」的意思。

normal.en: Consecutive days, consecutive years and consecutive wins all count things with no gap.
normal.cn: 连续几天、连续数年与连胜，数的都是没有缺口的事物。

normal.en: Consecutive numbers are neighbours on the number line, like adjacent seats in a row.
normal.cn: 连号数字是数轴上的邻居，就像一排里相邻的座位。

normal.en: A consecutive clause is named for the result that follows from the main statement.
normal.cn: 结果从句得名于由主句陈述引出的结果。

normal.en: Consecutive interpreting follows speech in chunks, one stretch after another.
normal.cn: 交替传译跟着讲话分段进行，一段接一段。

abstract.en: A gap is the only enemy of this word: if one day is missing, the run is broken.
abstract.cn: 缺口是这个词唯一的敌人：只要缺了一天，连续就断了。

abstract.en: Time is not a line but a stack of pages, and consecutive means no page was torn out.
abstract.cn: 时间不是一条线，而是一叠纸页，连续就意味着没有一页被撕掉。

abstract.en: A streak is fragile because it is counted backwards; one loss erases the whole series.
abstract.cn: 连续纪录之所以脆弱，是因为它被倒着数；一场失利就抹掉整串。

examples.en: The region suffered three consecutive summers of drought.
examples.cn: 该地区连续三个夏天遭遇干旱。

examples.en: Her consecutive victories surprised the whole circuit.
examples.cn: 她的连胜让整个巡回赛都感到意外。

examples.en: Number the pages in consecutive order from front to back.
examples.cn: 把书页从前往后按连续顺序编号。

core.cn: 核心意象：日历一叠页接连翻过，每个日期都紧贴下一个，中间没有空白页。

branches.en: THE UNBROKEN STRETCH: time or a count runs on with nothing missing.
branches.cn: 不间断的一段：时间或计数一路延续，什么都不缺。

branches.en: THE RUN AND THE SERIES: wins stack up, and neighbouring items share an edge.
branches.cn: 连续纪录与序列：胜利层层累积，相邻各项共用一条边。

branches.en: THE CHAIN OF CAUSES: one event follows another as its outcome.
branches.cn: 因果链：一个事件作为结果跟随另一个事件。

branches.en: THE GRAMMATICAL RESULT: a clause states what follows from the main clause.
branches.cn: 语法上的结果：从句陈述由主句引出的内容。

branches.en: THE WORKING AND CLIMATE RECORD: unbroken shifts, and statistics over year after year.
branches.cn: 作业与气候记录：连续的班次，以及逐年累积的统计。

intro.en: Emeritus is Latin emeritus, having served out one time, from e- meaning out and meritus meaning earned, the past participle of merere, to deserve.
intro.cn: emeritus 就是拉丁语 emeritus（已服满役期），由 e-（出）与 meritus（挣得的）构成，后者是 merere（应得）的过去分词。

items.en: Merere means to deserve or to earn, and gives English merit.
items.cn: merere 意为应得或挣得，给出英语 merit。

items.en: Meritus is the past participle, meaning earned or deserved.
items.cn: meritus 是过去分词，意为挣得的或应得的。

items.en: Emeritus means having served out one time, said of a soldier discharged with honour.
items.cn: emeritus 意为已服满役期，用于光荣退伍的士兵。

items.en: English takes emeritus in the 1700s for a retired officer or clergyman who keeps his title.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪吸收 emeritus，指保留头衔的退休军官或教士。

items.en: Universities adopt professor emeritus for a retired chair who keeps the rank.
items.cn: 大学采用 professor emeritus 指保留职级的退休讲席教授。

items.en: The Latin forms emerita and emeriti appear for women and for groups.
items.cn: 拉丁形式 emerita 与 emeriti 出现，分别用于女性与群体。

note.en: Emeritus, merit and meritorious share the Latin root merere, to deserve; retired and honorary are the nearest everyday words.
note.cn: emeritus、merit 与 meritorious 共享拉丁词根 merere（应得）；retired 与 honorary 是最接近的日常用词。

dict_mnemonic.text: emeritus ＝ e-（出）＋ meritus（挣得的，拉丁 merere「应得」的过去分词）＝「已服满役期、功成身退」。原是拉丁语，直接借入英语。拉丁式复数 emeriti（阳性或混合）、阴性单数 emerita、阴性复数 emeritae；英语也可写 emerituses。同根 merit 功绩、meritorious 有功的、demerit 过失、meritocracy 精英体制。用法：作形容词常后置 professor emeritus 荣誉退休教授，前置 emeritus professor 也常见，另有 emeritus status 荣誉退休身份、emeritus of history 历史学荣誉退休教授；作名词指人 an emeritus 一位荣誉退休者、the emeriti 全体荣誉退休人员。近义 retired 只说退休，honorary 指未经实际任职而授予的荣誉头衔；emeritus 特指实际任满、退休后保留原头衔。注意重音在第二音节。

由「结构」加形容词词尾构成，义为「结构的」
由「结构的」加副词词尾构成，义为「结构上」
由拉丁语「一起建造」构成，义为「建造」
由「建造」加表示结果的名词词尾构成，义为「建造、施工」
由拉丁语「在内建造」构成，义为「指导、教导」
由拉丁语「巧思」经法语进入英语，义为「工程师」

senses.title: The branch that checks load paths
senses.definition: the branch of engineering that analyses how loads travel through a structure and whether every member can carry them
senses.definitionCN: 分析荷载如何在结构中传递、每个构件能否承担的分析分支
senses.example: Structural engineering decides which member carries which load.
senses.exampleCN: 结构工程决定哪个构件承担哪一份荷载。
senses.why: Structural marks the frame, engineering marks the profession, so the phrase names the branch that reads the frame.
senses.whyCN: 「结构的」标出框架，「工程」标出专业，因此这个词组指解读框架的分支。

senses.title: Loads and forces
senses.definition: the calculation of dead, live, wind and seismic loads and the forces they produce
senses.definitionCN: 计算恒载、活载、风载与地震荷载及其产生的内力
senses.example: Structural engineering added the wind load that the first design ignored.
senses.exampleCN: 结构工程补上了初版设计忽略的风荷载。
senses.why: Before a member can be sized, its loads must be known, so load study is the branch's first task.
senses.whyCN: 构件定尺寸之前必须先知道荷载，因此荷载研究是该分支的首要任务。

senses.title: Steel design
senses.definition: the sizing and connection of steel beams, columns and frames
senses.definitionCN: 钢梁、钢柱与钢框架的选型与连接设计
senses.example: Structural engineering chose a steel frame for the long span.
senses.exampleCN: 结构工程为这一大跨度选择了钢框架。
senses.why: Steel carries tension well, so the branch uses it where spans must be light and long.
senses.whyCN: 钢材抗拉性能好，该分支便把它用在需要轻而长的跨度处。

senses.title: Concrete structures
senses.definition: the design of reinforced concrete beams, slabs and columns
senses.definitionCN: 钢筋混凝土梁、板与柱的设计
senses.example: Structural engineering placed the reinforcement where tension appears.
senses.exampleCN: 结构工程把钢筋放在出现拉力的位置。
senses.why: Concrete is strong in compression but weak in tension, so the branch adds steel where it is pulled.
senses.whyCN: 混凝土抗压好而抗拉弱，该分支便在受拉处加钢筋。

senses.title: Seismic design
senses.definition: the detailing of structures so that they bend without collapsing during an earthquake
senses.definitionCN: 细部设计使结构在地震中变形而不倒塌
senses.example: Structural engineering let the frame sway rather than break.
senses.exampleCN: 结构工程让框架摇摆而不是断裂。
senses.why: A structure can survive a quake by yielding in planned places, and that planning is the branch's job.
senses.whyCN: 结构可在地震中通过有计划的部位屈服而存活，这种规划正是该分支的工作。

senses.title: Strengthening existing structures
senses.definition: the assessment and retrofit of old buildings that must carry new loads
senses.definitionCN: 评估并改造需要承担新荷载的旧建筑
senses.example: Structural engineering strengthened the floor before the new machines arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 结构工程在新机器运来之前加固了楼板。
senses.why: Old frames often outlive their original use, so the branch also works backwards on what already stands.
senses.whyCN: 旧框架常比原用途活得更久，因此该分支也反过来处理已建成的东西。

senses.title: Bridge structures
senses.definition: the design of bridge decks, girders, arches and cables
senses.definitionCN: 桥面、主梁、拱与索的设计
senses.example: Structural engineering tuned the cable forces of the new footbridge.
senses.exampleCN: 结构工程调校了新人行桥的索力。
senses.why: A bridge is a frame whose whole purpose is to span, so it is a favourite object of the branch.
senses.whyCN: 桥梁是专为跨越而设的框架，因此是该分支最常处理的对象。

senses.title: The degree and the consultant
senses.definition: the university training and the professional practice that certify structural engineers
senses.definitionCN: 培养并认证结构工程师的大学训练与专业实务
senses.example: He took structural engineering after his first degree in civil works.
senses.exampleCN: 他在取得土木工程本科学位后攻读结构工程。
senses.why: The branch has its own advanced training and its own consultants, so the phrase also names a career.
senses.whyCN: 该分支有自己的进阶训练与顾问，因此这个词组也指一种职业。

intro.en: Structural engineering joins a Latin noun for building with the profession word from ingenium; it names the branch that asks whether a frame can stand.
intro.cn: 「结构工程」把拉丁语中表示「建造」的名词，与源自「巧思」的专业词组合；它命名的是追问框架能否站住的分支。

items.en: Struere meant to build, to pile up or to arrange in layers; it is the direct Latin source, while its own earlier root is a reconstruction often, but not certainly, linked to a spreading root.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语动词指建造、堆叠或分层排列；它是本词的直接拉丁语来源，其更早词根属重构性质，常被联结到表示「铺展」的词根，但并无确证。

items.en: Structura named the act and result of building, and English took it as structure for both the frame and its arrangement.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词指建造的行为与结果，英语以「结构」接收它，既指框架也指其安排方式。

items.en: The adjective structural appeared in the nineteenth century for what belongs to a frame or to the arrangement of parts.
items.cn: 「结构的」这一形容词在十九世纪出现，指属于框架或部件安排方式的。

items.en: Ingenium meant natural ability; French engin, a clever device, produced English engineer.
items.cn: 这个拉丁语名词指天赋；法语中指精巧装置的一词产生了英语「工程师」。

items.era: NINETEENTH CENTURY SPLIT · FIRST RECORD DATE UNCERTAIN
items.en: As iron, steel and reinforced concrete made frames calculable, structural work separated from general civil engineering as its own branch; the exact year of first record is uncertain.
items.cn: 随着铁、钢与钢筋混凝土使框架可计算，结构工作从普通土木工程中分离出来，成为独立分支；具体首见年代不确定。

items.en: The phrase now covers load analysis, member design, seismic detailing and the assessment of existing buildings and bridges.
items.cn: 这个词组如今涵盖荷载分析、构件设计、抗震细部与既有建筑及桥梁的评估。

note.en: The first group shares the build root; the second group names nearby design fields and ideas.
note.cn: 第一组共享「建造」词根；第二组是相邻的设计领域与概念。

entries.definition: The frame or arrangement itself; the phrase names the branch that designs it.
entries.definitionCN: 框架或安排本身；词组指设计它的分支。

entries.definition: Of a frame or of parts arranged together; it is the first half of the target.
entries.definitionCN: 框架的、部件安排的；是目标词组的前半。

entries.definition: To build by putting parts together; it shares the root but names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 把部件组合起来建造；共享词根，但指动作。

entries.definition: To build knowledge into someone; the same root with a different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 把知识建进某人心中；同词根不同前缀。

entries.definition: The wider field that includes structures among roads, water and ground works.
entries.definitionCN: 更宽的领域，结构只是道路、水利与岩土工作之一。

entries.definition: Describing a part that carries weight; an idea inside the branch, not the branch itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述承担重量的部件；是分支内的概念，而非分支。

entries.definition: The physical study of stress and strain; it supplies the branch's theory.
entries.definitionCN: 研究应力与应变的物理学；为该分支提供理论。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes and real fixed terms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Structure comes from a Latin verb meaning to build in layers.
normal.cn: 「结构」来自一个表示分层建造的拉丁语动词。

normal.en: The family runs structure, structural, construct, construction, instruct.
normal.cn: 同族词包括结构、结构的、建造、施工、指导。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: structural engineering analysis, structural engineering software.
normal.cn: 固定搭配可标记它：结构工程分析、结构工程软件。

normal.en: Its daily question is simple: can this frame carry that load?
normal.cn: 它的日常问题很简单：这个框架能承担那份荷载吗？

normal.en: Its answers are written in steel, concrete, timber and cable.
normal.cn: 它的答案写在钢、混凝土、木材与索上。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of hands where every hand must hold the weight passed to it.
abstract.cn: 想象一串手，每只手都必须接住传过来的重量。

abstract.en: Picture a tree that bends in a storm rather than snapping at the trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树在风暴中弯曲，而不是在树干处折断。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge that tells the river below exactly where its weight goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥清楚地告诉下方的河，它的重量去了哪里。

examples.en: Structural engineering explains why the balcony needed a second beam.
examples.cn: 结构工程解释了这座阳台为何需要第二根梁。

examples.en: The structural engineering report listed every overloaded joint.
examples.cn: 结构工程报告列出了每个超载节点。

examples.en: She teaches structural engineering to third-year civil students.
examples.cn: 她给三年级土木学生教授结构工程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「结构」+「工程」——把每一份重量沿框架送到地面

root: 前半源自拉丁语「分层建造」的结果名词，后半源自拉丁语「巧思」经法语的「工程师」；建造一词更早的来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one question: where does the weight go? The phrase covers load paths, loads, steel, concrete, earthquakes, repair, bridges and the profession.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕一个问题：重量去哪里？这个词组覆盖传力路径、荷载、钢材、混凝土、地震、加固、桥梁与职业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a frame bending slightly under a load and passing it along members until the ground takes it.
core.cn: 核心意象：框架在荷载下微微弯曲，把力沿构件逐段传递，直到地面接住它。

branches.en: THE METHOD: finding the load path and calculating the loads that travel along it.
branches.cn: 方法：找出传力路径并计算沿路径传递的荷载。

branches.en: THE STEEL VERSION: light frames for long spans.
branches.cn: 钢材版本：用于大跨度的轻质框架。

branches.en: THE CONCRETE VERSION: mass in compression with steel where tension appears.
branches.cn: 混凝土版本：受压的实体，在受拉处配钢筋。

branches.en: THE RESISTANCE VERSION: planned yielding in earthquakes and strengthening of old frames.
branches.cn: 抗力版本：地震中有计划的屈服，以及旧框架的加固。

branches.en: THE SPANNING AND PROFESSIONAL VERSION: bridges and the certified consultant.
branches.cn: 跨越与职业版本：桥梁与持证顾问。

intro.en: Both halves are Latin-rooted: one from a verb of layered building, one from the word for cleverness behind engineer.
intro.cn: 两半都是拉丁语词根：一半来自分层建造的动词，一半来自「工程师」背后的「巧思」。

latinIntro.en: Latin struere and structura supply the frame half; ingenium supplies the profession half.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「建造」与「结构」提供框架一半，「巧思」提供专业一半。

items.example: It forms construct, to build together.
It forms instruct, to build in.
It carried the root to English.

definition_zh: 石灰岩；以碳酸钙为主要成分的沉积岩
definition_en: a sedimentary rock made mainly of calcium carbonate, often formed from the shells and skeletons of marine organisms
core_image: 溶洞壁上被水溶出沟槽的灰白色层状岩石
scene: 溶洞入口的岩壁上留着水滴溶出的沟槽，导游用手电照出层理： The cave walls are made of limestone that rainwater has slowly dissolved.
sceneCN: 这里 limestone 指「以碳酸钙为主的沉积岩」（第 1 个义项：主要由碳酸钙构成的沉积岩）；句意为洞壁由雨水缓慢溶蚀的石灰岩构成。

pos.zh: 石灰岩（物质名词；指不同种类时复数为 limestones）

senses.title: A sedimentary rock of calcium carbonate
senses.titleCN: 以碳酸钙为主的沉积岩
senses.definition: a sedimentary rock composed chiefly of calcium carbonate, usually built up from shell debris or chemical precipitation
senses.definitionCN: 主要由碳酸钙组成、通常由贝壳碎屑或化学沉淀堆积而成的沉积岩
senses.example: The cave walls are made of limestone that rainwater has slowly dissolved.
senses.exampleCN: 洞壁由雨水缓慢溶蚀的石灰岩构成。
senses.why: Lime plus stone names the rock by its chief product: burn it and you get lime, the binder of mortar.
senses.whyCN: lime 加 stone 以主要产物给岩石命名：烧炼它便得到石灰，也就是灰浆的胶结料。

senses.title: Building stone cut from beds
senses.titleCN: 作为建筑石材的石灰岩
senses.definition: the rock used as dimension stone for walls, floors, and monuments
senses.definitionCN: 用作墙体、地面与纪念碑块材的该种岩石
senses.example: The old church was built of pale limestone blocks.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老教堂用浅色石灰岩块砌成。
senses.why: Because it cuts easily and hardens on exposure, limestone became a standard building stone wherever beds were thick.
senses.whyCN: 由于易于切割且暴露后会变硬，只要层厚足够，石灰岩就成了标准建筑石材。

senses.title: A bed or formation of the rock
senses.titleCN: 作为层位或地层的石灰岩
senses.definition: a distinct layer or body of limestone within a rock sequence
senses.definitionCN: 岩层序列中一层或一套明确的石灰岩体
senses.example: A thick limestone bed separates the two shale units.
senses.exampleCN: 一层厚石灰岩把两套页岩隔开。
senses.why: As a mass noun it names material; as a count noun it names one bed of that material.
senses.whyCN: 作物质名词时指材料，作可数名词时指该材料的一个层位。

senses.title: Karst terrain shaped by solution
senses.titleCN: 溶蚀形成的喀斯特地貌
senses.definition: the landscape of caves, sinkholes, and pavements produced when the rock is dissolved by acidic water
senses.definitionCN: 酸性水溶蚀该岩石后形成的洞穴、落水洞与溶蚀台地景观
senses.example: Limestone country is full of sinkholes and dry valleys.
senses.exampleCN: 石灰岩地区遍布落水洞与干谷。
senses.why: The rock's weakness is also its signature: it dissolves, so its landscape is a map of water paths.
senses.whyCN: 这种岩石的弱点也是它的标志：它会溶解，因此其地貌就是水路的地图。

senses.title: Raw material for cement and lime
senses.definition: the rock quarried and heated to make cement, mortar, and agricultural lime
senses.definitionCN: 经开采与煅烧以制造水泥、灰浆与农用石灰的岩石
senses.example: The plant grinds limestone into raw meal for cement.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂把石灰岩磨成水泥生料。
senses.why: Industry names the rock by what it yields: calcium carbonate becomes quicklime when heated.
senses.whyCN: 工业按产出物命名岩石：碳酸钙受热即变为生石灰。

senses.title: Fossil-rich limestone
senses.definition: limestone that preserves shells, corals, or other hard parts of marine life
senses.definitionCN: 保存贝壳、珊瑚或其他海洋生物硬体的石灰岩
senses.example: The flagstones are full of fossil shells.
senses.exampleCN: 这些铺石上满是化石贝壳。
senses.why: Much limestone is literally accumulated skeletons, so the rock doubles as a record of ancient seas.
senses.whyCN: 许多石灰岩实际上就是堆积的骨骼，因此这种岩石同时是古海洋的记录。

senses.title: Chalk as a soft variety
senses.definition: a soft, fine-grained, white variety of limestone made of microscopic shell plates
senses.definitionCN: 由微小壳体片堆积而成、柔软细粒的白色石灰岩变种
senses.example: The white cliffs are chalk, a very pure limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 白色崖壁是白垩，一种很纯的石灰岩。
senses.why: Chalk is limestone written in miniature: the same chemistry, built from far smaller skeletons.
senses.whyCN: 白垩是缩小版的石灰岩：化学成分相同，只是由小得多的骨骼堆成。

senses.title: A soil-forming parent material
senses.definition: limestone bedrock that weathering turns into thin, alkaline soils
senses.definitionCN: 经风化变为薄层碱性土壤的石灰岩基岩
senses.example: The thin soil over limestone supports dry grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 石灰岩上的薄土养育着干性草地。
senses.why: Rock becomes soil; because this rock is alkaline, its soils are basic and often thin.
senses.whyCN: 岩石化为土壤；由于这种岩石偏碱性，其土壤呈碱性且往往很薄。

senses.title: Abstract: a archive of ancient life
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：远古生命的档案
senses.definition: something that preserves a readable record of past conditions in layered form
senses.definitionCN: 以层状形式保存过去状况、可供解读的记录物
senses.example: The reef limestone is an archive written by living things.
senses.exampleCN: 这座礁石灰岩是一部由生物写成的档案。
senses.why: The metaphor uses the rock's origin: layer upon layer of shells is a record accumulated by living bodies, not by ink.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻利用岩石的成因：一层层贝壳是由生物体而非墨水累积成的记录。

intro.en: Limestone is an English compound of lime and stone. Its parts are native, while the geological sense is early modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: limestone 是 lime 与 stone 的英语复合词。两部分均为本族语，地质义形成于近代早期。年代均为约数。

items.en: Lim meant a sticky substance, mortar, or birdlime, from Proto-Germanic limaz. The same root is behind Latin limus 'mud', which is related rather than directly ancestral.
items.cn: lim 原指黏性物质、灰浆或粘鸟胶，来自原始日耳曼语 limaz。同一词根也见于拉丁语 limus「泥」，二者是旁系关系而非直接祖孙。

items.en: Heating limestone produces quicklime, so lime came to name both the product and the rock that yields it.
items.cn: 煅烧石灰岩可得到生石灰，因此 lime 既指产物，也指产出它的岩石。

items.en: The compound limestone appears in Middle English for the rock, distinguishing it from lime the substance.
items.cn: 复合词 limestone 见于中古英语，用来指这种岩石，以区别于物质性的 lime。

items.en: Chemistry later identified the rock as calcium carbonate, and the adjective calcareous was borrowed from Latin calx 'lime'.
items.cn: 化学后来确认这种岩石是碳酸钙，形容词 calcareous 借自拉丁语 calx「石灰」。

items.en: Nineteenth-century study of the Kras region made limestone the type rock of solution landscapes; the term karst dates from that work.
items.cn: 19 世纪对喀斯特地区的研究使石灰岩成为溶蚀地貌的典型岩石，karst 一词即源于这项工作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first citation): the earliest written use of the compound in English is not precisely dated, and the deeper origin of lim is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见书证）：该复合词在英语中的最早书面使用没有精确年代，lim 的更深来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds rock names that are constantly mistaken for limestone; group two holds materials and products that share its chemistry.
note.cn: 第一组是常被误认为石灰岩的岩石名称；第二组是化学成分相关的材料与产物。

entries.definition: The burnt product calcium oxide or the sticky substance; in geology it is not the rock itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指煅烧产物氧化钙或黏性物质；在地质语境中并不是岩石本身。

entries.definition: Rock made of sand grains, usually quartz; it is clastic, not built from shells or chemical precipitate.
entries.definitionCN: 由砂粒、通常为石英构成的岩石；属碎屑岩，不由贝壳或化学沉淀构成。

entries.definition: A carbonate rock in which magnesium partly replaces calcium; it looks like limestone but reacts more slowly with acid.
entries.definitionCN: 镁部分取代钙的碳酸盐岩；外观似石灰岩，但与酸反应更慢。

entries.definition: A soft white limestone of microscopic shell plates; it is a kind of limestone, not a separate chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 由微小壳板构成的软白石灰岩；它是石灰岩的一种，化学成分并非另一类。

entries.definition: Limestone recrystallized by heat and pressure; it is the metamorphic product, not the sediment.
entries.definitionCN: 经热与压力重结晶的石灰岩；它是变质产物，而非沉积物。

entries.definition: The compound that makes up the rock; the mineral name calcite is used for its crystalline form.
entries.definitionCN: 构成该岩石的化合物；其结晶形态的矿物名为方解石。

entries.definition: Calcium sulfate, a softer mineral that also forms white beds; it is not a carbonate.
entries.definitionCN: 硫酸钙，一种较软的矿物，也形成白色层位；它不是碳酸盐。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real rock names and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实语素、真实岩石名称与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Lime + stone: burn the stone and you get lime, the oldest clue to its identity.
normal.cn: lime 加 stone：烧这种石头就得到石灰，这是识别它最古老的线索。

normal.en: Limestone is mostly calcium carbonate, so acid makes it bubble.
normal.cn: 石灰岩主要是碳酸钙，因此遇酸会起泡。

normal.en: Its family runs limestone, lime, limy, calcareous and calcium.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 limestone、lime、limy、calcareous 与 calcium。

normal.en: Karst landscapes are the signature of limestone: caves, sinkholes, dry valleys.
normal.cn: 喀斯特地貌是石灰岩的标志：洞穴、落水洞、干谷。

normal.en: Chalk and marble are limestone's soft and hardened cousins.
normal.cn: 白垩与大理岩是石灰岩的软、硬两位表亲。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are made of old seashells.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，书架都由古老贝壳做成。

abstract.en: Picture a stone that answers acid with a fizz, like a cough.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头遇酸以气泡作答，像一声咳嗽。

abstract.en: Picture a landscape drained by hidden pipes, all of them dissolved by rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一片由隐蔽管道排水的土地，所有管道都是雨水溶出来的。

examples.en: The cave walls are made of limestone that rainwater has slowly dissolved.
examples.cn: 洞壁由雨水缓慢溶蚀的石灰岩构成。

examples.en: Builders cut limestone blocks from the bed beside the river.
examples.cn: 工匠从河边岩层中切出石灰岩块。

examples.en: Because limestone neutralizes acid, farmers spread crushed rock on sour fields.
examples.cn: 由于石灰岩能中和酸，农民把碎石撒在酸性田里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「莱姆斯通」——烧一烧就变成石灰的石头 → 石灰岩

root: 英语 lime「石灰、黏性物质」（古英语 lim，原始日耳曼语 limaz）+ stone「石头」；属英语本族复合词。化学上主要成分为碳酸钙，拉丁语 calx「石灰」给出 calcareous。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one rock from its chemistry to its beds, its caves, its quarries, its fossils, its soils, and finally to its use as an image of a layered archive.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项让同一种岩石从化学成分走到层位、洞穴、采石场、化石、土壤，最后成为层层档案的意象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pale layered rock with water-cut grooves, soft enough for rain to hollow it out.
core.cn: 核心意象：浅色层状岩石上有水溶出的沟槽，软得能被雨水掏空。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND BED: the same substance is both a mass noun and a countable layer.
branches.cn: 材料与层位：同一物质既可作物质名词，也可作可数的一层。

branches.en: STONE AND PRODUCT: it is cut for walls and burned for cement, two uses of one chemistry.
branches.cn: 石材与产物：既被切作墙体，也被烧作水泥，是同一化学的两种用途。

branches.en: SOFTNESS: solubility and fine shell plates make caves, pavements and chalk cliffs.
branches.cn: 软质：可溶性与细壳板共同造出洞穴、台地与白垩崖。

branches.en: RECORD: shells become rock, and the rock becomes a readable archive.
branches.cn: 记录：贝壳变成岩石，岩石又成为可读的档案。

branches.en: PARENT MATERIAL: weathering turns the rock into thin alkaline soil.
branches.cn: 母质：风化把岩石变成薄层碱性土壤。

intro.en: The compound is made of two native English nouns, but its chemistry adds a Latin adjective.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个英语本族名词构成，但其化学性质带来一个拉丁语形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin calx 'lime' supplies calcareous and calcium; the English compound itself has no Latin source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 calx「石灰」提供 calcareous 与 calcium；英语复合词本身没有拉丁语源。

items.example: Lime mortar holds the old bricks together.
items.exampleCN: 石灰砂浆把旧砖粘在一起。

items.example: The wall is built of local stone.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙用本地石材砌成。

items.example: The quarry yields a hard grey limestone.
items.exampleCN: 这座采石场出产坚硬的灰色石灰岩。

items.example: The limy soil supports chalk grassland.
items.exampleCN: 含石灰的土壤养育白垩草地。

items.meaning: made of or containing calcium carbonate

items.example: Calcium carbonate is the main mineral.

items.structure: Old English cealc, from Latin calx
items.example: Chalk is a pure form of limestone.
items.exampleCN: 白垩是石灰岩的一种纯净形态。

items.example: Marble is limestone recrystallized by heat.
items.exampleCN: 大理岩是受热重结晶的石灰岩。

items.structure: German Karst, from the Kras plateau
items.exampleCN: 喀斯特在石灰岩溶解处形成。

definition_zh: adj. 雄辩的；有说服力的；意味深长的；明白显示出的
definition_en: fluent and forceful in speech; showing feeling or proof clearly without many words
core_image: 法庭上律师不再追问，只把一张空椅子的照片举给陪审团看，旁听席一片安静；讲台上一个人两手空空却句句落地；旧照片里一只搭在肩上的手
scene: 法庭上律师没有再追问，只把那张空椅子的照片举起来给陪审团看，旁听席一片安静。 The empty chair was eloquent enough to end the argument.
sceneCN: 这里 eloquent 指「清楚证明某事的，用于事实或迹象」（第 3 个义项：明白显示出的）；句意是那张空椅子足以说明问题，结束了争论。图中可辨识物件：空椅子照片、陪审席、安静的旁听席。

pos.zh: 雄辩的；有说服力的；意味深长的；明白显示出的

senses.title: Fluent and persuasive
senses.definition: fluent and forceful in speech, able to persuade
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）言辞流畅有力、能说服人的
senses.example: She gave an eloquent speech without once looking at her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了一场雄辩的演讲，一次也没看稿子。
senses.why: A speaker with both hands free and a closed notebook lying on the lectern.
senses.whyCN: 演讲者两手都空着，讲台上放着一本合起的笔记本。

senses.title: Expressing feeling clearly
senses.definition: showing feeling clearly without needing many words
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）无需多言就清楚传达感情的
senses.example: One eloquent look from her mother stopped the question at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 母亲一个意味深长的眼神，让餐桌上的问题停住了。
senses.why: A raised eyebrow across a dinner table with a fork paused halfway to a mouth.
senses.whyCN: 餐桌对面挑起的一道眉毛，一把叉子停在半路。

senses.title: Giving clear evidence
senses.definition: giving clear proof of something, used of facts or signs
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）清楚证明某事的，用于事实或迹象
senses.example: The empty chair was eloquent enough to end the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 那张空椅子足以说明问题，结束了争论。
senses.why: A photograph of one empty chair held up before a silent jury box.
senses.whyCN: 一张空椅子的照片被举到安静的陪审席前。

intro.en: Eloquent is Latin eloquens, the participle of eloqui, which joins ex- meaning out to loqui meaning to speak; it describes someone who speaks out well.
intro.cn: eloquent 就是拉丁语 eloquens，eloqui 的分词，而 eloqui 把 ex-（向外）与 loqui（说话）结合；它形容把话说得好的人。

items.en: Latin loqui means to speak.
items.cn: 拉丁语 loqui 意为说话。

items.en: Adding ex- gives eloqui, to speak out.
items.cn: 加 ex- 构成 eloqui，意为说出来。

items.en: The participle eloquens means speaking out well.
items.cn: 分词 eloquens 意为把话说得好的。

items.en: English took eloquent in the 14C for a persuasive speaker.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借用 eloquent，指有说服力的演讲者。

items.en: Writers applied eloquent to looks, gestures and silence.
items.cn: 作家把 eloquent 用于眼神、手势与沉默。

items.en: Lawyers used eloquent for facts that prove a point without argument.
items.cn: 律师用 eloquent 指无需论证就能说明问题的事实。

note.en: Eloquent and loquacious share loqui, the Latin root for speak; eloquent speaks well and persuades, loquacious simply speaks a great deal.
note.cn: eloquent 与 loquacious 共用 loqui，那是拉丁语「说话」的词根；eloquent 说得好且能说服人，loquacious 只是说得多。

entries.definition: fluent persuasive speech
entries.definitionCN: 口才；雄辩

entries.definition: in a fluent and persuasive way
entries.definitionCN: 雄辩地

entries.definition: talking a great deal
entries.definitionCN: 话多的；健谈的

entries.definition: able to express ideas clearly and fluently
entries.definitionCN: 表达清楚的；口齿伶俐的

entries.definition: able to make someone believe or act
entries.definitionCN: 有说服力的

entries.definition: showing feeling or meaning clearly
entries.definitionCN: 富表情的；意味深长的

normalIntro.cn: 五个「无需多言就能说话」的画面。

dict_mnemonic.text: eloquent ＝ e-（向外）＋ loqu（说话，拉丁 loqui）＋ -ent（形容词后缀）＝「能把话说出来的」。名词 eloquence，副词 eloquently。三层用法按「谁在说」分：人 an eloquent speaker 雄辩的演讲者；言辞 an eloquent speech 雄辩的演讲；无声之物 eloquent silence 意味深长的沉默、an eloquent look 传情的一瞥、eloquent proof 明白有力的证据。固定结构 eloquent of ＋ 名词＝「明白显示出…」：a face eloquent of despair 一张写满绝望的脸。比较级用 more eloquent，没有 eloquenter。近义 articulate 强调表达清楚有条理，persuasive 强调能说服，expressive 强调表情达意；loquacious 只是话多，未必说得好。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外）＋ loqui（说话）→ eloqui → eloquens（善言的）→ eloquent（雄辩的）
