intro.cn: eloquent 由 e- 加 loqu- 加 -ent 组成；-ence 给出 eloquence，-ly 给出 eloquently，artic- 给出 articulate，press- 给出 expressive。

latinIntro.en: Latin loqui means to speak, articulus a small joint and suadere to urge; these roots give eloquent, articulate and persuasive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 loqui 意为说话，articulus 意为小关节，suadere 意为劝告；这些词根给出 eloquent、articulate 与 persuasive。

definition_zh: 血流；血液循环；（体内的）血液
definition_en: the blood flowing through the body's vessels, considered as one continuous stream
core_image: 血液在全身血管里像一条河流一样不断流动
scene: 这里指「血流」。 The drug reaches the bloodstream within twenty minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 bloodstream 指「血液循环」（第 3 个义项：进入并在全身血流中运行）；句意：药物在二十分钟内进入血液循环。图中可辨识物件：血管剖面、药片、血流箭头、计时器。

pos.zh: 血流；血液循环；体内的血液（通常作单数，前面加 the）

senses.title: The circulating blood
senses.titleCN: 血液循环：体内不断流动的血液整体
senses.definition: the blood moving continuously through the arteries, veins and capillaries
senses.definitionCN: 在动脉、静脉与毛细血管中持续流动的血液整体
senses.example: The heart keeps the bloodstream moving day and night.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏让血液循环日夜不停。
senses.why: The compound joins blood to stream, picturing the whole circulation as one river rather than separate vessels.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 blood 与 stream 结合，把整套循环想象成一条河，而不是一根根分开的管子。

senses.title: The blood as a medium
senses.titleCN: 血液：作为运输介质的体液
senses.definition: the blood regarded as the medium that carries oxygen, nutrients, hormones and waste
senses.definitionCN: 把血液看作运送氧气、养分、激素与废物的介质
senses.example: Glucose dissolves in the bloodstream and is carried to cells.
senses.exampleCN: 葡萄糖溶在血液中，被送到细胞。
senses.why: Once pictured as a stream, the blood becomes a medium in which things dissolve and travel.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被想象成河流，血液就变成一种可以把东西溶入并带走的介质。

senses.title: Entering the circulation
senses.titleCN: 进入血液循环：药物或养分入血
senses.definition: the route by which a substance passes into the circulating blood
senses.definitionCN: 物质进入循环血液的途径
senses.example: The drug reaches the bloodstream within twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 药物在二十分钟内进入血液循环。
senses.why: Pharmacology needs a destination phrase, and 'the bloodstream' names the compartment a substance must reach to act.
senses.whyCN: 药理学需要一个「目的地」说法，而 the bloodstream 正是物质要到达才能起效的隔室。

senses.title: Concentration in blood
senses.titleCN: 血中浓度：血液里某物的水平
senses.definition: the level of a substance present in the circulating blood at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻循环血液中某物质的水平
senses.example: Insulin levels in the bloodstream rise after a meal.
senses.exampleCN: 饭后血液中的胰岛素水平升高。
senses.why: Measurement made the stream a sampling site, so the word appears in phrases about levels and concentrations.
senses.whyCN: 测量让这条「河流」成为取样点，因此这个词出现在关于水平与浓度的短语中。

senses.title: Spread through blood
senses.titleCN: 经血流传播：感染或细胞随血扩散
senses.definition: the route by which infection, toxins or cancer cells travel around the body
senses.definitionCN: 感染、毒素或癌细胞在全身扩散的途径
senses.example: Bacteria in the bloodstream can cause sepsis.
senses.exampleCN: 血液中的细菌可能引发败血症。
senses.why: Because the stream reaches every tissue, it becomes the body's highway for harm as well as for supply.
senses.whyCN: 因为这条「河流」到达每个组织，它既是供应线，也是伤害的通道。

senses.title: Bloodstream infection
senses.titleCN: 血流感染：血液中出现病原体
senses.definition: a clinical condition in which microorganisms are present and growing in the blood
senses.definitionCN: 微生物在血液中存在并繁殖的临床状态
senses.example: A bloodstream infection requires immediate antibiotics.
senses.exampleCN: 血流感染需要立即使用抗生素。
senses.why: Microbiology needed a compartment name to say where the organisms are growing, and the stream supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学需要一个隔室名称来说明病原体在哪里繁殖，而 bloodstream 正好提供了这样一个名称。

senses.title: Flow and speed
senses.definition: the rate at which blood moves through the circulation as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 血液在整个循环中移动的快慢
senses.example: Exercise speeds up the bloodstream and warms the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 运动加快血流并使皮肤变暖。
senses.why: Stream carries the idea of current, so the word can describe rate as well as contents.
senses.whyCN: stream 带有「水流」之意，因此这个词既可指内容物，也可指流速。

senses.title: Everything carried in blood
senses.titleCN: 血液运载物：氧气、糖、激素与废物
senses.definition: the set of substances in transit in the blood at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 任一时刻在血液中运输的全部物质
senses.example: The bloodstream carries carbon dioxide back to the lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 血液循环把二氧化碳送回肺部。
senses.why: The stream image makes the blood a container of cargo, so one word can cover every substance in transit.
senses.whyCN: 河流意象把血液变成装载货物的容器，因此一个词就能涵盖一切在运输中的物质。

senses.title: A figurative mainstream
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：进入主流或系统内部
senses.definition: figuratively, the main channel of a system, as when an idea enters the mainstream
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某个系统的主渠道，如某种观点进入主流
senses.example: The idea entered the bloodstream of the industry within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法一年之内进入了行业的主流。
senses.why: Once the stream is the body's main channel, any system's main channel can borrow the image.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这条河流成为身体的主渠道，任何系统的主渠道都能借用这个意象。

intro.en: Bloodstream is an English compound of blood, from Old English blod, and stream, from Old English stream. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: bloodstream 是英语复合词，由古英语 blod「血」与古英语 stream「水流」构成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Blod is the native Germanic word for blood; its deeper Indo-European links are reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: blod 是表示血的本族日耳曼词；其更深的印欧语联系属重构，并无记录。

items.en: Stream meant a flowing current of water. The metaphor of a bodily river was available as soon as the two words were joined.
items.cn: stream 指流动的水流。两个词一结合，身体里有一条河的比喻就自然成立。

items.en: The compound bloodstream is recorded in the nineteenth century, when physiology began describing the circulation as a single moving system. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合词 bloodstream 记录于 19 世纪，当时生理学开始把循环描述成一个整体流动系统。最早的确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine fixed phrases such as bloodstream infection and levels in the bloodstream, treating the circulation as a measurable compartment.
items.cn: 20 世纪医学固定了 bloodstream infection、levels in the bloodstream 等短语，把循环视为可测量的隔室。

items.en: Journalism extended the word beyond the body, so that trends and ideas can enter the bloodstream of an organisation.
items.cn: 新闻写作把这个词扩展到身体之外，使潮流与观念也能进入某个组织的主流。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first citation is uncertain, and the deeper origins of both blod and stream are reconstructions, not recorded forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：最早书证年代存疑；blod 与 stream 的更深来源均属重构形式，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds the container-and-content words that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the circulation and its flow.
note.cn: 第一组是「容器与内容物」之间容易混淆的词；第二组是「循环及其流动」的近义词。

entries.definition: A tube that carries blood; bloodstream names what flows inside those tubes.
entries.definitionCN: 运送血液的管道；bloodstream 指管道里流动的东西。

entries.definition: The fluid tissue itself; bloodstream adds the idea of continuous circulation.
entries.definitionCN: 指血液这种流体组织本身；bloodstream 增加了持续循环的意思。

entries.definition: The movement of blood around the body; bloodstream can mean either the moving blood or the system it forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指血液在全身的运动；bloodstream 既可指流动的血液，也可指它构成的系统。

entries.definition: A specific diagnosis, not a synonym for the blood itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一个具体诊断，并不是血液本身的同义词。

entries.definition: The whole loop of heart, vessels and blood; it stresses the circuit rather than the fluid.
entries.definitionCN: 指心脏、血管与血液构成的整个环路，强调回路而非流体。

entries.definition: The movement of blood through a vessel or organ, often measured in volume per minute.
entries.definitionCN: 血液通过某条血管或某个器官的运动，常以每分钟体积计量。

entries.definition: The network of vessels itself; the bloodstream is what the network carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指血管网络本身；bloodstream 是该网络运送的内容。

entries.definition: The clear fluid left after blood clots; it is a laboratory fraction, not the circulating whole.
entries.definitionCN: 血液凝固后剩下的清液，是实验室组分，不是循环中的全血。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: blood + stream: blood pictured as a river running through the body.
normal.cn: blood + stream：把血液想象成流经全身的一条河。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: enter the bloodstream, bloodstream infection, in the bloodstream.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：进入血液、血流感染、在血液中。

normal.en: The family runs blood, bleed, bloody, blood-borne and bloodstream.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 blood、bleed、bloody、blood-borne、bloodstream。

normal.en: blood vessel is the container; bloodstream is the contents.
normal.cn: blood vessel 是容器，bloodstream 是内容物。

normal.en: The phrase usually takes 'the': the bloodstream.
normal.cn: 这个短语通常加 the：the bloodstream。

abstract.en: Picture a river network inside the body, with the heart as its pumping station.
abstract.cn: 想象体内一张河流网络，心脏是它的泵站。

abstract.en: Picture a pill dissolving and its molecules riding the current to every organ.
abstract.cn: 想象一片药溶解，分子随水流被带到每个器官。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour entering an organisation the way a solute enters the blood.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻进入某个组织，像溶质进入血液一样。

examples.en: Alcohol reaches the bloodstream within minutes of drinking.
examples.cn: 饮酒后几分钟内酒精就进入血液循环。

examples.en: The infection spread through the bloodstream to the joints.
examples.cn: 感染经血流扩散到关节。

examples.en: Doctors monitor drug levels in the bloodstream to avoid toxicity.
examples.cn: 医生监测血液中的药物浓度以避免毒性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「blood 血 + stream 河流」——血液像河一样在体内流动 → bloodstream 血液循环

root: 古英语 blod「血」+ 古英语 stream「水流」→ 英语复合词 bloodstream。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one current: blood is pictured as a river that supplies every tissue, carries drugs and germs, can be sampled, and can finally stand for the mainstream of any system.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一股水流展开：血液被想象成一条河，供应每个组织、运送药物与病菌、可被取样，最后也能代表任何系统的主流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous river of blood running through the whole body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条贯穿全身、连续流动的血液之河。

branches.en: THE RIVER AND ITS CARGO: the circulating whole, the medium, and everything in transit.
branches.cn: 河流与货物：循环整体、介质，以及一切在运输中的东西。

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL AND THE READING: a substance enters, and then its level is measured.
branches.cn: 到达与读数：物质先进入，随后其水平被测量。

branches.en: THE HIGHWAY OF HARM: germs travel by blood, and bloodstream infection names the result.
branches.cn: 伤害的高速路：病菌经血传播，血流感染则命名其结果。

branches.en: THE CURRENT'S SPEED: the stream image also gives the word a rate.
branches.cn: 水流的速度：河流意象也赋予这个词一个速率。

branches.en: OUT OF THE BODY: the metaphor leaves anatomy and names the main channel of any system.
branches.cn: 离开身体：这个比喻脱离解剖，命名任何系统的主渠道。

intro.en: Bloodstream is a native compound of two Old English words, with no Latin suffix in its own structure.
intro.cn: bloodstream 是两个古英语词构成的本族复合词，自身结构中没有拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: The compound has no Latin source; its scientific relatives come from Latin vas 'vessel' and Greek haima 'blood', as in vascular and hematology.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有拉丁来源；它的科学同族词来自拉丁 vas「容器」与希腊 haima「血」，如 vascular 与 hematology。

items.example: The toxin entered the bloodstream quickly.
items.exampleCN: 毒素很快进入血液循环。

items.meaning: the red fluid of the body
items.example: Blood carries oxygen to the brain.
A stream ran beside the path.
The wound bled for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 伤口流了一个小时的血。
血液学涵盖贫血与凝血。

definition_zh: 胚胎学；对胚胎及其发育的研究
definition_en: the branch of biology that studies embryos and their development
core_image: 一排玻璃皿里躺着从单细胞到成形幼体的序列，像一条把时间摊开来看的走廊
scene: 在发育生物学实验室里，教授指着培养箱说： Embryology traces how a single cell becomes a complex organism.
sceneCN: 这里 embryology 指「研究胚胎及其发育的学科」（第 1 个义项：胚胎学）；句意是胚胎学追踪单个细胞如何变成一个复杂的生物体。

pos.zh: 胚胎学
对胚胎发育的研究

senses.title: The science of embryos
senses.definition: the branch of biology that studies embryos and their development
senses.definitionCN: 研究胚胎及其发育的生物学分支
senses.example: Embryology traces how a single cell becomes a complex organism.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎学追踪单个细胞如何变成一个复杂的生物体。
senses.why: Embryon is the Greek word for a young one still growing, and -logia is study, so the noun names the discipline first.
senses.whyCN: embryon 是希腊语中指仍在生长的幼体，-logia 是研究，因此这个名词首先指学科。

senses.title: The development of an embryo
senses.definition: the process by which an embryo forms and grows
senses.definitionCN: 胚胎形成与生长的过程
senses.example: The embryology of the frog was observed day by day.
senses.exampleCN: 青蛙的胚胎发育被逐日观察。
senses.why: Like other -ology nouns, it can name the object of study, so embryology also means the development being studied.
senses.whyCN: 与其他 -ology 名词一样，它也可指研究对象，因此 embryology 也指被研究的发育过程。

senses.title: The embryological account of a species
senses.titleCN: 某一物种的胚胎发育叙述
senses.definition: the particular developmental history of a given species
senses.definitionCN: 某一特定物种的胚胎发育史
senses.example: The embryology of the sea urchin is unusually well documented.
senses.exampleCN: 海胆的胚胎发育记录得格外详尽。
senses.why: Narrowing from the science to one species gives a species-specific account of how its young form.
senses.whyCN: 从学科收窄到一个物种，就得到该物种幼体如何形成的专门叙述。

senses.title: Comparative embryology
senses.definition: the comparison of embryonic development across species
senses.definitionCN: 跨物种比较胚胎发育的学问
senses.example: Comparative embryology once supplied key evidence for common descent.
senses.exampleCN: 比较胚胎学曾为共同祖先提供关键证据。
senses.why: Putting embryos of different animals side by side turns development into evolutionary evidence.
senses.whyCN: 把不同动物的胚胎并排摆放，就把发育变成演化证据。

senses.title: Medical embryology
senses.definition: the study of human embryonic development for clinical purposes
senses.definitionCN: 为临床目的研究人类胚胎发育的学问
senses.example: Medical embryology explains the origin of certain heart defects.
senses.exampleCN: 医学胚胎学解释了某些心脏缺陷的成因。
senses.why: Clinicians need the embryonic timeline to understand which structures can go wrong and when.
senses.whyCN: 临床医生需要胚胎时间表，才能理解哪些结构会在何时出错。

senses.title: Plant embryology
senses.definition: the study of embryos within seeds and their formation
senses.definitionCN: 研究种子内胚胎及其形成的学问
senses.example: Plant embryology begins with the fertilized egg inside the ovule.
senses.exampleCN: 植物胚胎学从胚珠内的受精卵开始。
senses.why: Plants keep their embryos inside seeds, so their embryology follows a different physical route.
senses.whyCN: 植物把胚胎留在种子里，因此其胚胎学走的是另一条物理路径。

senses.title: Embryological evidence for evolution
senses.titleCN: 支持演化的胚胎学证据
senses.definition: the use of shared embryonic features as evidence of relatedness
senses.definitionCN: 用共享的胚胎特征作为亲缘关系证据
senses.example: Embryology was cited long before genes could be compared.
senses.exampleCN: 在能够比较基因之前，胚胎学就已被援引。
senses.why: Similar embryos in different animals suggest a shared developmental programme inherited from a common ancestor.
senses.whyCN: 不同动物相似的胚胎提示一套从共同祖先继承来的发育程序。

senses.title: An academic course or textbook
senses.definition: the taught subject or textbook treatment of embryonic development
senses.definitionCN: 作为教学科目或教材内容的胚胎发育
senses.example: Embryology is taught in the second year of the medical curriculum.
senses.exampleCN: 胚胎学在医学课程的第二年讲授。
senses.why: A research field becomes a subject with lectures and chapters, and the same noun covers that classroom form.
senses.whyCN: 一个研究领域会成为有讲座与章节的科目，同一个名词也覆盖这种课堂形态。

intro.en: Embryology joins Greek embryon young one to -logia study; embryon itself is built from en- in and bryein to swell, and the deeper origin of bryein is uncertain.
intro.cn: embryology 把希腊 embryon「幼体」与 -logia「研究」结合；embryon 本身由 en-「在内」与 bryein「膨胀」构成，bryein 的更深来源不确定。

items.en: Embryon meant a young one still forming, and also a swelling; the literal image is something growing inside.
items.cn: embryon 意为仍在形成的幼体，也指肿块；字面意象是某物在里面生长。

items.en: En- meant in, and bryein meant to swell or be full; the compound pictured life swelling inside a container.
items.cn: en- 意为「在内」，bryein 意为「膨胀、充满」；复合词描绘生命在容器内膨胀。

items.en: Logia, from logos, named the study or account of a subject.
items.cn: logia 出自 logos，指对某主题的研究或论述。

items.en: Modern Latin embryologia assembled embryon and -logia as a name for the study of embryonic development.
items.cn: 近代拉丁 embryologia 把 embryon 与 -logia 组装起来，作为研究胚胎发育的名称。

items.en: English embryology spread in the nineteenth century as comparative and experimental studies of development expanded.
items.cn: 随着发育的比较与实验研究扩张，英语 embryology 在 19 世纪传播开来。

items.en: Source uncertain as to the root: the deeper origin of Greek bryein is unresolved, so any Indo-European base offered for it is a reconstruction; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（bryein 词根存疑、年代为约数）：希腊 bryein 的更深来源尚无定论，凡为其给出的印欧语基形式均属重构形式；英语首见年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the embryo root that are often confused with the discipline name; group two holds neighbouring fields that also study development.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 embryo 词根、常与学科名混淆的词；第二组是同样研究发育的相邻领域。

entries.definition: The developing organism itself; embryology is the study of it, not the thing studied.
entries.definitionCN: 正在发育的生物体本身；embryology 是对它的研究，而非被研究之物。

entries.definition: Relating to an embryo; it describes a structure or stage, while embryology names a field.
entries.definitionCN: 与胚胎有关的；它描述结构或阶段，而 embryology 指学科。

entries.definition: A person who studies embryos; the -ist form is the practitioner of embryology.
entries.definitionCN: 研究胚胎的人；-ist 形式是 embryology 的从业者。

entries.definition: A biological variant of embryonic, used mainly in technical descriptions of embryonic tissue.
entries.definitionCN: embryonic 的生物学异体，主要用于描述胚胎组织的技术文本。

entries.definition: The broader study of how organisms grow; embryology is its classic embryo-focused core.
entries.definitionCN: 研究生物如何生长的更广领域；胚胎学是其以胚胎为核心的经典部分。

entries.definition: The study of developmental abnormalities; it shares embryology's timeline but focuses on defects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究发育异常的学问；共享胚胎学的时间线，但聚焦缺陷。

entries.definition: The study of body structure; embryology explains how that structure comes to exist.
entries.definitionCN: 研究身体结构的学问；胚胎学解释该结构如何形成。

entries.definition: The study of tissues; embryonic tissue is one of its early subjects.
entries.definitionCN: 研究组织的学问；胚胎组织是其早期研究对象之一。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Embryon young one plus -logia study: the study of the forming young.
normal.cn: embryon「幼体」加 -logia「研究」：研究正在形成的幼体。

normal.en: The family runs embryo, embryonic, embryology, embryologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 embryo、embryonic、embryology、embryologist。

normal.en: Comparative, experimental, medical and plant embryology are fixed branches.
normal.cn: 比较、实验、医学与植物胚胎学是固定分支。

normal.en: The field is tied to a timeline: fertilization, cleavage, gastrulation, organ formation.
normal.cn: 这门学科绑在一条时间线上：受精、卵裂、原肠形成、器官发生。

normal.en: Medical embryology explains birth defects by asking when a structure failed.
normal.cn: 医学胚胎学通过追问某结构何时出错来解释出生缺陷。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor of glass dishes, each holding one moment of the same life.
abstract.cn: 想象一条玻璃皿走廊，每只皿装着同一生命的一个瞬间。

abstract.en: Picture a film played one frame at a time until a shape appears.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影逐格播放，直到出现一个形状。

abstract.en: Picture a seed opening into a map of what it will become.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子打开成一张它将变成什么的图。

examples.en: She read a classic paper in experimental embryology before starting the experiment.
examples.cn: 开始实验之前，她读了一篇实验胚胎学的经典论文。

examples.en: Embryology and genetics now meet in the study of development.
examples.cn: 胚胎学与遗传学如今在发育研究中相遇。

examples.en: The museum's embryology collection includes specimens from a century ago.
examples.cn: 博物馆的胚胎学藏品包括一个世纪前的标本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「embryo 胚胎 + ology 学科」——研究胚胎如何形成的学问 → 胚胎学

root: 希腊 embryon「幼体；肿块」= en-「在内」+ bryein「膨胀」+ -logia「研究」，经近代拉丁 embryologia；bryein 更深来源不确定，英语首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the discipline to the development it studies, then to one species, one comparative method, one medical use, one botanical setting, one evolutionary argument and one classroom.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从学科走向它所研究的发育，再走向单个物种、比较方法、医学用途、植物场景、演化论证与课堂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a corridor of dishes holding one life at successive moments, time laid out side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条摆着玻璃皿的走廊，同一生命的不同瞬间被并排摊开。

branches.en: FIELD AND PROCESS: the study of embryos and the development studied share one name.
branches.cn: 学科与过程：对胚胎的研究与被研究的发育共享一个名称。

branches.en: ONE SPECIES: each organism has its own documented embryonic history.
branches.cn: 单个物种：每种生物都有自己记录在案的胚胎史。

branches.en: COMPARISON: embryos placed side by side become evidence of relatedness.
branches.cn: 比较：并排摆放的胚胎成为亲缘关系的证据。

branches.en: APPLIED SETTINGS: hospitals and seed banks ask different embryological questions.
branches.cn: 应用场景：医院与种子库提出不同的胚胎学问题。

branches.en: ARGUMENT AND LESSON: the field supplies both an evolutionary argument and a course.
branches.cn: 论证与课程：这门学科既提供演化论证，也提供一门课程。

intro.en: Embryology is a Greek compound of a noun about young life and a suffix about study, and both pieces recur across biology.
intro.cn: embryology 是一个希腊复合词，由指幼体生命的名词与指研究的后缀构成，两个部件在生物学中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Greek embryon gives embryo and embryonic; Greek -logia, from logos, gives the names of disciplines such as embryology and histology.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 embryon 给出 embryo 与 embryonic；希腊 -logia 出自 logos，给出 embryology、histology 等学科名。

items.example: The prefix places the growing thing inside.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把生长之物置于内部。

items.example: The verb gives the image of swelling life.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出生命膨胀的意象。
这个后缀命名一门学科。
胚胎学追踪细胞的路径。

items.example: The embryo has a tiny root.
items.exampleCN: 这个胚胎有一条微小的根。
胚胎学家对标本作了分期。

definition_zh: n. 商品；有用的东西
definition_en: a raw material or product that can be bought and sold
core_image: 成袋的咖啡豆堆在交易所大厅里
scene: 咖啡豆在全球市场上是一种重要商品。 Coffee beans are a major commodity on world markets.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：commodity 指商品；句意是咖啡豆在全球市场上是一种重要商品。

pos.zh: 商品；有用的东西

senses.title: A tradable product
senses.definition: a raw material or basic product traded in bulk
senses.definitionCN: 大宗交易的原料或基本产品
senses.example: Oil is the world's most traded commodity.
senses.exampleCN: 石油是世界上交易量最大的商品。
senses.why: Latin commoditas meant convenience, then advantage.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 commoditas 意为便利，后指好处。

senses.title: Anything useful and valued
senses.definition: something valuable that people want or need
senses.definitionCN: 人们想要或需要的宝贵之物
senses.example: Clean water is a precious commodity here.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里干净的水是珍贵之物。
senses.why: The figurative sense treats value as merchandise.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义把「价值」当作货物。

intro.en: Commodity began as a word for convenience and advantage.
intro.cn: commodity 最初指便利与好处。

items.en: Commodus means convenient or suitable.
items.cn: commodus 意为便利、合适。

items.en: Commoditas means convenience, then advantage.
items.cn: commoditas 意为便利，后指好处。

items.en: Commodity meant a benefit or profit.
items.cn: 十五世纪 commodity 意为益处或利润。

items.en: It came to mean goods for sale.
items.cn: 十八世纪它指待售货物。

items.en: Commodity now names raw materials.
items.cn: 现代 commodity 指原材料。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the commod- shape; the near-meaning group names things sold.
note.cn: 形近组共享 commod- 词形；近义组列出可售之物。

entries.definition: Roomy and convenient.
entries.definitionCN: 宽敞的。

entries.definition: A chest of drawers.
entries.definitionCN: 五斗柜。

entries.definition: A naval officer rank.

definition_zh: 入侵部队；侵略军；登陆编队
definition_en: the whole body of troops, ships and aircraft assembled to carry out an invasion, or any major part of it
core_image: 河口外的锚地，运输船与护航舰排成长列，甲板上停着车辆与箱笼，岸线在雾里只露一道浅灰
scene: 河口外的锚地，运输船与护航舰排成长列，甲板上停着车辆。 The invasion force assembled in the estuary and waited for calm weather.
sceneCN: 这里 invasion force 指「为实施入侵而集结的整支武装力量」（第 1 个义项：入侵部队整体）；句意为入侵部队在河口集结，等待天气转稳。场景物件：运输船、护航舰、甲板车辆、锚地。

pos.zh: 入侵部队；侵略军；登陆编队

senses.title: The whole body assembled to invade
senses.titleCN: 为入侵集结的整支部队
senses.definition: all the troops, ships and aircraft gathered to carry out one invasion
senses.definitionCN: 为执行一次入侵而汇集的所有兵员、舰船与飞机
senses.example: The invasion force assembled in the estuary and waited for calm weather.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵部队在河口集结，等待天气转稳。
senses.why: the phrase joins the name of the act to the name of the body, so it can hold an entire expedition in two words.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把行为之名与力量之名接在一起，两个词就装下整场远征。

senses.title: The landing troops
senses.definition: the soldiers or marines who are put ashore first, as distinct from the ships that carry them
senses.definitionCN: 最先上岸的士兵或陆战队员，与运送他们的舰船相区别
senses.example: The invasion force came ashore in four waves before the tide turned.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵部队在潮水转向之前分四批上岸。
senses.why: because a landing is the decisive moment, the phrase often narrows to the men on the beaches.
senses.whyCN: 由于登陆是决定性时刻，这个短语常收窄到海滩上的人。

senses.title: The fleet that carries them
senses.definition: the ships and landing craft that move and supply the troops
senses.definitionCN: 运送与补给兵员的舰船与登陆艇
senses.example: The invasion force lay offshore for two days under radio silence.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵舰队在无线电静默下于近海停了两天。
senses.why: naval usage lets the same phrase name the floating half of the expedition, since without it no landing happens.
senses.whyCN: 海军用法让同一短语指远征中漂浮的那一半，因为没有它就没有登陆。

senses.title: The air component
senses.definition: the aircraft and airborne units that support or precede the landing
senses.definitionCN: 支援或先于登陆的飞机与空降部队
senses.example: The invasion force included night bombers and two airborne divisions.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵编队包括夜间轰炸机与两个空降师。
senses.why: twentieth-century warfare made air power part of the body, so the phrase grew a third arm.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的战争让空中力量成为这支队伍的一部分，短语由此长出第三条臂膀。

senses.title: The joint command organisation
senses.definition: the headquarters and staff that control the whole operation
senses.definitionCN: 控制整个行动的司令部与参谋机构
senses.example: The invasion force had its own signal company and weather officer.
senses.exampleCN: 入侵部队有自己的通信连与气象军官。
senses.why: staff language treats the command as the force itself, because the body cannot move without it.
senses.whyCN: 参谋语言把指挥机构当作部队本身，因为没有它这具躯体动不了。

senses.title: A named historical expedition
senses.definition: a particular invasion force remembered under a campaign name or a date
senses.definitionCN: 以战役名或年代被记住的某支入侵部队
senses.example: The Norman invasion force carried horses, prefabricated forts and a duke.
senses.exampleCN: 诺曼入侵部队带着马匹、预制堡垒和一位公爵。
senses.why: historians turn one assembly into a proper name, and the phrase becomes a chapter heading.
senses.whyCN: 史家把一次集结变成专名，这个短语于是成了章节标题。

senses.title: A mass arrival, used loosely
senses.definition: any large group whose arrival feels like an occupation
senses.definitionCN: 任何到来时像占领一样的大群人
senses.example: An invasion force of tourists took every table by one o'clock.
senses.exampleCN: 到一点钟，一支由游客组成的入侵部队已占满每张桌子。
senses.why: journalists borrow the military phrase for comic effect, and the exaggeration is the point.
senses.whyCN: 记者借用这个军事短语制造滑稽效果，夸张本身就是要点。

senses.title: A fictional or game army
senses.titleCN: 虚构或推演中的入侵军团
senses.definition: an invading army in a novel, film, wargame or strategy game
senses.definitionCN: 小说、电影、兵棋或策略游戏中的入侵军队
senses.example: The scenario gives each player one invasion force and one winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个推演给每位玩家一支入侵部队和一个冬天。
senses.why: games and fiction keep the phrase because it instantly supplies a side, a goal and a supply line.
senses.whyCN: 游戏与虚构保留这个短语，因为它立刻提供一方、一个目标与一条补给线。

intro.en: Invasion force is an English phrase joining invasion, from Latin invasio, to force, from Old French force and Latin fortis 'strong'.
intro.cn: invasion force 是英语短语，把 invasion（来自拉丁 invasio）与 force（来自古法语 force、拉丁 fortis「强」）接在一起。

items.en: Invasion is Latin invasio 'a going into, an attack', the noun of invadere, built on in- 'into' and vadere 'to go'.
items.cn: invasion 是拉丁 invasio「进入、攻击」，即 invadere 的名词，由 in-「进入」与 vadere「走」构成。

items.en: Force came through Old French force from Late Latin fortia, a noun of strength built on fortis 'strong'.
items.cn: force 经古法语 force 来自晚期拉丁 fortia，这是由 fortis「强」构成的「力量」名词。

items.en: The phrase settled in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries as staff language for the whole body assembled to seize a coast or a country.
items.cn: 这个短语在 19 与 20 世纪固定为参谋用语，指为夺取海岸或国家而集结的整支部队。

items.en: Because a landing needs ships, aircraft and troops, the phrase can name the whole or any major part, and context decides.
items.cn: 由于登陆需要舰船、飞机与兵员，这个短语可指全体，也可指任一主要部分，由语境决定。

items.en: Journalists also use it for any large hostile-seeming arrival, from insects to tourists.
items.cn: 记者也用它指任何看似敌意的大批到来，从昆虫到游客。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the phrase has no single documented coinage, and its earliest military use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这个短语没有单一可考的最早造词，其最早军事用例只能约略定年。

note.en: Group one holds compounds built on force; group two holds other names for a body sent to fight abroad.
note.cn: 第一组是以 force 构成的复合词；第二组是派往海外作战之部队的其他名称。

entries.definition: A group assembled for a specific operation; it need not be an invasion and may be small.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定行动组建的队伍；不一定是入侵，规模也可能很小。

entries.definition: A standing branch of a nation's military, not an expedition gathered for one landing.
entries.definitionCN: 国家常设军种，不是为一次登陆而集结的远征。

entries.definition: The present-participle variant describes the body while it acts; the noun phrase names it as a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词变体描述正在行动的部队；名词短语则把它当作一个事物来命名。

entries.definition: On its own it means strength or an organised body; the compound narrows it to one purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时指力量或有组织的队伍；复合后收窄到单一目的。

entries.definition: Troops sent to a distant theatre for a campaign, whether or not they invade.
entries.definitionCN: 派往远方战区的部队，无论是否入侵。

entries.definition: A large fleet, often used historically or rhetorically; it covers ships only.
entries.definitionCN: 庞大的舰队，常用于历史或修辞语境；只涵盖舰船。

entries.definition: A small detachment put ashore for a limited task, much smaller than an invasion force.
entries.definitionCN: 为有限任务上岸的小分队，比入侵部队小得多。

entries.definition: Soldiers stationed to hold a place already taken, the opposite of a body sent to take one.
entries.definitionCN: 驻扎守住已占之地的士兵，与派去攻取的部队正相反。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: a real compound, a real Latin root behind force and real campaign names.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合结构、force 背后真实的拉丁词根与真实战役名。

normal.en: invasion + force: the act plus the body that performs it.
normal.cn: invasion + force：行为加上执行它的那具躯体。

normal.en: force goes back to fortis 'strong', which also gives fort, fortify and effort.
normal.cn: force 上承 fortis「强」，还给出 fort、fortify、effort。

normal.en: The phrase can name the troops, the ships, the aircraft or the command, and context decides.
normal.cn: 这个短语可指兵员、舰船、飞机或指挥机构，由语境决定。

normal.en: History supplies the example: the Norman invasion force of 1066.
normal.cn: 历史提供例子：一〇六六年的诺曼入侵部队。

normal.en: Modern loose use turns tourists into an invasion force, with the joke carried by the exaggeration.
normal.cn: 现代宽松用法把游客变成入侵部队，笑点由夸张承担。

examples.cn: 这支入侵部队需要平静的水面，胜过需要更多人手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因维申福斯」听似「硬围身、复死」——硬围上来、拼命往前压的一整队人 → 入侵部队

root: 英语短语：invasion（拉丁 invasio，出自 in- + vadere）+ force（古法语 force，上承晚期拉丁 fortia、fortis「强」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses divide one expedition into its parts: the whole body, the landing troops, the fleet, the aircraft, the command, a named historical case, a joking crowd and a game army.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一支远征拆成几部分：全体、登陆兵员、舰队、航空部分、指挥机构、有专名的历史个案、戏谑的人潮与游戏中的军团。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: transports and escorts in a long line at anchor, vehicles on deck, a grey coast in fog.
core.cn: 核心意象：运输船与护航舰在锚地排成长列，甲板上停着车辆，雾中只有一道灰色的海岸。

branches.en: WHOLE AND HEAD: the assembled expedition and its headquarters are named by the same phrase because neither moves without the other.
branches.cn: 全体与首脑：整支远征与其司令部用同一短语命名，因为缺一皆不能动。

branches.en: MEN AND SHIPS: the troops on the beach and the fleet offshore are the two halves of one landing.
branches.cn: 人与船：海滩上的兵员与近海的舰队，是一次登陆的两半。

branches.en: AIR: twentieth-century warfare added a third arm to the body.
branches.cn: 空中：20 世纪的战争给这具躯体加上第三条臂膀。

branches.en: HISTORY: one assembly becomes a proper name and a chapter heading.
branches.cn: 历史：一次集结变成专名与章节标题。

branches.en: BORROWED BODIES: tourists and game armies borrow the phrase, one for a joke and one for a scenario.
branches.cn: 借用的躯体：游客与游戏军团都借用这个短语，一为玩笑，一为推演。

intro.en: Invasion force is a two-word English phrase whose halves come from Latin and French, and each half has its own family.
intro.cn: invasion force 是一个两词英语短语，两半分别来自拉丁与法语，各自都有词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin vadere 'to go' stands behind invasion, and Latin fortis 'strong' stands behind force through Late Latin fortia and Old French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vadere「走」是 invasion 的底；拉丁 fortis「强」经晚期拉丁 fortia 与古法语成为 force 的底。

definition_en: to pay no attention to something, or a lack of attention or respect for it

senses.definition: to pay no attention to advice, warnings or facts
senses.definitionCN: （动词）对建议、警告或事实毫不留意

senses.exampleCN: 他不理会警示标志，继续干活。

senses.title: Lack of respect

senses.why: A fence driven straight through a footpath.

intro.en: Disregard is dis- plus regard, and regard comes from Old French regarder, to look at, from re- plus garder, to watch or guard, which is of Germanic origin; to disregard is to stop looking.
intro.cn: disregard 由 dis- 加 regard 构成，而 regard 来自古法语 regarder「看」，由 re- 加 garder「看守、注视」组成，后者源自日耳曼语；disregard 就是不再看一眼。

items.cn: 古法语 garder 意为看守、注视。

items.en: Regarder means to look at or look back at.

items.en: Disregard appears for the absence of that attention.

items.en: The noun and verb are both common in formal reports.

note.en: Disregard is not looking; its look-alikes keep the watch root, and its neighbours name other ways of letting something pass unnoticed.

definition_zh: 纳税人；纳税的个人或企业；（作定语）由纳税人负担的
definition_en: a person or organization that is required by law to pay taxes to a government
core_image: 四月里邮局柜台前的一叠报税表，每张表后面都站着一个要交钱的人
scene: 每年四月，街角邮局里排队寄表的人格外多。 Every April the queue at the corner post office is full of taxpayers mailing their returns.
sceneCN: 每年四月，街角邮局里排队寄表的人格外多；句中的 taxpayers 指「按法律申报并缴纳个人所得税的人」（第 1 个义项：个人所得税纳税人）。图中可辨识物件：报税表、信封、邮局柜台、排队的背影。

pos.zh: 纳税人；纳税的个人或企业
由纳税人负担的；纳税人的

senses.title: A person who files and pays income tax
senses.titleCN: 申报并缴纳个人所得税的人
senses.definition: an individual who is legally required to report income and pay tax on it
senses.definitionCN: 依法须申报收入并就其缴纳个税的个人
senses.example: Every April the queue at the corner post office is full of taxpayers mailing their returns.
senses.exampleCN: 每年四月，街角邮局里排队寄表的人格外多，都是寄报税表的纳税人。
senses.why: Tax names the charge and payer names the one who settles it, so a single word marks the person on the paying side of the fiscal relation.
senses.whyCN: tax 指这笔课征，payer 指付清它的人，合起来就标记出财政关系里付钱的一方。

senses.title: A company or body that pays tax
senses.definition: a business or institution legally liable for tax on its profits, property or activities
senses.definitionCN: 就利润、财产或经营活动依法负税的企业或机构
senses.example: The levy falls on corporate taxpayers with plants in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这项课征落在本地区设有工厂的企业纳税人身上。
senses.why: Fiscal law treats a company as a person for tax purposes, so the same word covers a firm as well as an individual.
senses.whyCN: 税法在税务上把公司当作一个「人」，因此同一个词既指个人也指企业。

senses.title: The taxed public, seen against government
senses.titleCN: 与政府相对的纳税公众
senses.definition: the body of citizens considered as the source of public money, especially in political argument
senses.definitionCN: 在政治争论中被视为公共资金来源的公民整体
senses.example: The mayor asked taxpayers to judge the plan at the next hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 市长请纳税人在下一次听证会上评判这项计划。
senses.why: Once tax funding became the normal source of public services, the word turned into a political name for the paying side.
senses.whyCN: 当税收成为公共服务的常规财源，这个词就变成政治语境里「付钱一方」的称呼。

senses.title: Whoever ends up bearing a public cost
senses.titleCN: 最终替某项公共开支买单的人（比喻）
senses.definition: used figuratively for the people who ultimately bear the cost of a public project or mistake
senses.definitionCN: 比喻指最终承担某项公共工程或失误代价的人
senses.example: When the stadium overran its budget, local taxpayers picked up the bill.
senses.exampleCN: 体育场预算超支后，账单落到了当地纳税人头上。
senses.why: The literal payer of tax stands for anyone left holding the cost when public money runs short.
senses.whyCN: 字面上交税的人，被用来代替公共资金不足时被迫承担代价的任何人。

senses.title: A resident registered for local tax
senses.titleCN: 在辖区登记纳税的居民纳税人
senses.definition: a resident who is registered with a local authority and pays local taxes there
senses.definitionCN: 在地方当局登记并在当地纳税的居民
senses.example: Only residents registered as taxpayers in the district may vote on the school levy.
senses.exampleCN: 只有在本区登记为纳税人的居民才能就学校课征投票。
senses.why: Local revenue systems attach the word to a register, so taxpayer becomes a legal category tied to a place.
senses.whyCN: 地方财政制度把这个词挂在登记册上，纳税人因此成为与地点绑定的法律类别。

senses.title: Someone liable for one particular tax
senses.titleCN: 某一具体税种的纳税义务人
senses.definition: a person who is the legal subject of a specific duty, such as a property or land tax
senses.definitionCN: 某项具体税负的法律主体，如房产税或土地税的义务人
senses.example: Owners of the riverside plots become taxpayers under the new land levy.
senses.exampleCN: 根据新的土地课征，河岸地块的所有人成为纳税人。
senses.why: Each tax statute defines its own payer, so the word can be narrowed to whoever that statute names.
senses.whyCN: 每一部税法都自行界定付税人，因此这个词可以收窄到该法所指的那个人。

senses.title: The tax base as a group
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的纳税人群体与税基
senses.definition: the whole group of people and firms whose payments fund public spending, viewed as a pool
senses.definitionCN: 其缴款支撑公共支出的全部个人与企业，被看作一个池子
senses.example: A shrinking workforce means a smaller pool of taxpayers for the pension fund.
senses.exampleCN: 劳动人口萎缩意味着养老基金的纳税人池子变小。
senses.why: Counting payers together turns the word into a quantity that planners can measure and project.
senses.whyCN: 把付税人合起来数，这个词就变成一个规划者可以衡量与预测的数量。

senses.title: Used before a noun: paid for by taxpayers
senses.titleCN: 作定语：由纳税人出资的
senses.definition: placed before a noun to say that the thing named is financed by public tax money
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示所指数事物由公共税款出资
senses.example: The bridge was rebuilt with taxpayer money, not private capital.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是用纳税人的钱重建的，不是私人资本。
senses.why: The attributive use compresses a whole sentence about funding into a label attached to the object.
senses.whyCN: 定语用法把一整句关于出资的话压缩成贴在物件上的标签。

intro.en: Taxpayer joins two Latin-derived words: tax, from taxare 'to assess or charge', and payer, from pacare 'to settle or pacify'. The compound is an English formation of the modern fiscal state. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: taxpayer 由两个源自拉丁语的词合成：tax 出自 taxare「评估、课征」，payer 出自 pacare「平息、清偿」。这个复合词是近代财政国家形成后的英语构词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Taxare meant 'to assess, evaluate, charge', originally a frequentative of tangere 'to touch', as if a value were felt out by hand.
items.cn: taxare 意为「评估、估量、课征」，原是 tangere「触摸」的反复动词，仿佛用手摸出价值。

items.en: Medieval Latin taxa named an assessed charge, and the noun passed into English as a levy imposed by authority.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 taxa 指经评估确定的课征额，这个名词进入英语后指当局征收的税。

items.en: Pacare 'to pacify' developed the sense 'to settle a debt, satisfy a creditor', which became the everyday verb to pay.
items.cn: pacare「使平息」引申出「清偿债务、使债主满意」的意思，后来成为日常动词「付钱」。

items.en: English built taxpayer from tax plus payer, naming the person on the paying side once taxation became routine and bureaucratized.
items.cn: 英语用 tax 加 payer 造出 taxpayer，在征税变得常规化、官僚化之后，用来指付钱的一方。

items.en: The spread of income tax in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries made the word a standard political term, and the attributive use followed.
items.cn: 十九、二十世纪所得税的普及使这个词成为标准政治用语，定语用法也随之出现。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same tax stem but naming different things; group two holds words for people who pay or are counted by a revenue system.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「税」词干但所指不同的词；第二组是收入体系中付钱或被计入的人。

entries.definition: The compulsory payment or the statute that imposes it; taxpayer names the person, not the payment.
entries.definitionCN: 指强制缴纳的款项或课征法规；taxpayer 指人，不指款项。

entries.definition: An adjective for income or goods that fall within the scope of a tax, whether or not anyone actually pays.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指收入或货物在征税范围内，不论实际是否有人缴款。

entries.definition: The whole activity or system of raising revenue by taxes, not any single payer within it.
entries.definitionCN: 指整套征税活动或制度，不是其中某个付税人。

entries.definition: The adjective describing the public as people who pay tax, as in the taxpaying public.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述缴税的公众，如「纳税公众」。

entries.definition: A British term for someone who pays local property-based rates; narrower than taxpayer, which covers all taxes.
entries.definitionCN: 英式说法，指缴纳地方房产税的人；比涵盖各类税的 taxpayer 窄。

entries.definition: A person who submits a tax return; the emphasis is on the form, not on the money paid.
entries.definitionCN: 指提交报税表的人；重点在表格，不在缴款。

entries.definition: A member of a state with rights and duties; taxpayer picks out only the fiscal duty.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有权利与义务的国家成员；taxpayer 只挑出财政义务。

entries.definition: Someone who lives in a place; many residents are taxpayers, but the words mark different facts.
entries.definitionCN: 在某地居住的人；许多居民是纳税人，但两个词标记的是不同事实。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实的固定搭配与真实的同族词。

normal.en: Tax plus payer: the charge on one side, the one who settles it on the other.
normal.cn: 「税」加「付钱者」：一边是课征，一边是清偿它的人。

normal.en: The family runs taxpayer, taxpayers, taxpaying and taxpayer-funded.
normal.cn: 同族词有 taxpayer、taxpayers、taxpaying 与 taxpayer-funded。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: individual taxpayer, corporate taxpayer, taxpayer money.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：个人纳税人、企业纳税人、纳税人的钱。

normal.en: Payer comes from the Latin verb for settling a debt, not from the noun for money.
normal.cn: payer 出自拉丁语中「清偿债务」的动词，并非出自表示钱的名词。

normal.en: Budget debates pair it with spending: taxpayer money funds public services.
normal.cn: 预算辩论把它与支出配对：公共服务的资金来自纳税人的钱。

abstract.en: Picture a long queue where each person hands over a folded form and keeps the carbon copy.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长队，每人交出一张折好的表格，自己留下复写的那一联。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir fed by thousands of small pipes, each labelled with a household name.
abstract.cn: 想象一座水库由成千根细管供水，每根管子上都写着一个家庭的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt handed back to the person who paid, while the goods go to everyone.
abstract.cn: 想象收据交回给付钱的人，而货物送给所有人。

examples.en: The agency publishes a guide for first-time taxpayers each winter.
examples.cn: 该机构每年冬天为首次纳税的人发布指南。

examples.en: Corporate taxpayers may offset part of the loss against next year's profit.
examples.cn: 企业纳税人可用部分亏损抵扣来年利润。

examples.en: Voters complained that taxpayer money was spent on a private consultant.
examples.cn: 选民抱怨纳税人的钱花在了一名私人顾问身上。

root: 英语复合词：tax（出自拉丁 taxare「评估、课征」）+ payer（出自拉丁 pacare「平息、清偿」，即付钱者）；指依法缴税的个人或企业。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the paying side of a fiscal relation: the individual filer, the corporate payer, the public facing government, the figurative bearer of cost, the local registrant, the subject of one tax, the collective tax base, and the attributive label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿财政关系中付钱的一方展开：个人申报者、企业缴款者、与政府相对的公众、比喻中的买单者、地方登记纳税人、某一税种的义务人、作为整体的税基，最后是定语标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a queue of people handing folded forms across a counter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一队人隔着柜台递上折好的表格。

branches.en: WHO PAYS: the individual at the counter and the company treated as a person for tax both fill the same role.
branches.cn: 谁在付：柜台前的个人与税务上被视为「人」的公司，扮演同一个角色。

branches.en: TWO SIDES: government collects, the paying public is named as the other side of that relation.
branches.cn: 两边：政府征收，纳税公众被命名为这段关系的另一边。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE BILL: whoever is left holding a public cost inherits the name of the literal payer.
branches.cn: 比喻账单：最终替公共开支兜底的人，继承了字面付税人的名号。

branches.en: LEGAL SUBJECT: a register in a district and a clause in a tax statute both single out the liable person.
branches.cn: 法律主体：辖区登记册与税法条文都挑出应负义务的那个人。

branches.en: COUNTED POOL: many payers become a base planners can measure, then a label for what the money buys.
branches.cn: 可数的池子：众多付税人成为规划者可衡量的税基，再变成所购之物的标签。

intro.en: Taxpayer is an English compound whose two halves each descend from a Latin verb, so the word reads as two actions joined.
intro.cn: taxpayer 是英语复合词，两半各自源自一个拉丁动词，因此这个词读起来是两个动作的结合。

latinIntro.en: Latin taxare supplies tax, taxable and taxation; Latin pacare supplies pay, payment and payer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 taxare 给出 tax、taxable 与 taxation；拉丁 pacare 给出 pay、payment 与 payer。

definition_zh: 效度；有效性；正确性；可信度；有效期
definition_en: the quality of being based on truth or reason, or of being legally or logically acceptable
core_image: 一台天平两端各放一只砝码盘，指针稳稳停在正中，旁边压着一张盖了印章的证书
scene: 检验室里一台天平两端放上砝码，指针停在正中，旁边压着一张已盖章的证书。 The validity of the test depends on whether it measures what it claims to measure.
sceneCN: 这里指测量工具确实测到其所声称之物的程度（第 1 个义项：测量效度）；句意为这项测验的效度取决于它是否测到了自己声称要测的东西。图中可辨识物件：天平、砝码、指针、盖章证书。

pos.zh: 效度；有效性；正确性；有效期

senses.title: The quality of measuring the right thing
senses.definition: the degree to which a test or instrument measures what it is intended to measure
senses.definitionCN: 测验或仪器测到其预定测量对象的程度
senses.example: The validity of the test depends on whether it measures what it claims to measure.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测验的效度取决于它是否测到了自己声称要测的东西。
senses.why: Validus meant strong, and a valid test is one strong enough to stand as a true measure.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为强，而有效的测验就是强到能站住脚的真实测量。

senses.title: Legal force
senses.definition: the quality of being legally acceptable or enforceable
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上可被接受或可被执行的属性
senses.example: The lawyer questioned the validity of the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 律师质疑这份合同的有效性。
senses.why: Law was among the first places where a document had to be strong enough to hold.
senses.whyCN: 法律是最早要求文件「强到能站住」的领域之一。

senses.title: Soundness of an argument
senses.definition: the quality of being well founded in fact or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在事实或推理上有充分根据的属性
senses.example: No one doubted the validity of her argument.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人怀疑她的论点站不站得住。
senses.why: A claim that can stand up to attack keeps the same strength metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 一个经得起攻击的说法，用的仍是同一个「强度」比喻。

senses.title: Trustworthiness of data
senses.definition: the extent to which data or evidence can be relied on
senses.definitionCN: 数据或证据可以被信赖的程度
senses.example: The validity of the data was checked before publication.
senses.exampleCN: 数据在发表之前已核查过可信度。
senses.why: Data must stand before conclusions may lean on it, and the word names that standing.
senses.whyCN: 数据必须先站住，结论才能靠上去，这个词命名的正是这种站住。

senses.title: The period a document is good for
senses.definition: the period during which a document or ticket is officially acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 证件或票券在官方上仍可被接受的那段时间
senses.example: Please check the validity of your passport before booking.
senses.exampleCN: 订票之前请检查护照的有效期。
senses.why: A document's strength can expire, so the word also names the time it remains strong.
senses.whyCN: 文件的效力会到期，所以这个词也指它保持有效的那段时间。

senses.title: Logical validity
senses.definition: the property of an argument whose conclusion must follow from its premises
senses.definitionCN: 结论必然由前提推出的论证所具有的属性
senses.example: The validity of the argument rests on its form, not its content.
senses.exampleCN: 这个论证的有效性取决于形式，而不是内容。
senses.why: Logic borrowed the word for a form that holds whatever the subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学借这个词指一种无论内容如何都成立的形式。

senses.title: Internal validity
senses.definition: the degree to which a study can show that its treatment caused the observed change
senses.definitionCN: 一项研究能证明其处理造成了所观察变化的程度
senses.example: Internal validity asks whether the design really isolates the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 内部效度问的是：这个设计是否真的把原因单独隔了出来。
senses.why: Modern design splits validity into parts, and the inside of a study is one of them.
senses.whyCN: 现代设计把效度分成几部分，研究内部就是其中一部分。

senses.title: External validity
senses.definition: the degree to which a study's results can be extended beyond its own sample
senses.definitionCN: 研究结果能超出自身样本向外推广的程度
senses.example: External validity asks whether the result travels beyond the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 外部效度问的是：结果能否走出这个样本。
senses.why: A result that holds only inside the lab is strong there and weak outside, so the outside gets its own name.
senses.whyCN: 只在实验室内成立的结果，在里面强、在外面弱，于是「外面」也单独有了名字。

intro.en: Validity comes from Latin validitas, strength, from validus, strong, and valere, to be strong or be worth. The source is clear; the date of its first English record is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词源自拉丁 validitas「力量、有效」，来自 validus「强壮的」，更早为 valere「有力量、有价值」。词源清楚，最早英语记录的年代不确定。

items.en: Valere meant to be strong, to have force or to be worth something.
items.cn: valere 意为强、有力量，或值某个价。

items.en: Validus was the adjective for strong or able to hold, and it stands behind the whole family.
items.cn: validus 是表示强壮、站得住的形容词，整个词族都由它而来。

items.en: Late Latin validitas named the quality of being strong, a word built with the abstract ending -itas.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 validitas 用表示性质的后缀命名「强」这一性质。

items.en: French validite carried the word into English with the sense of legal force.
items.cn: 法语 validite 把这个词带进英语，义为法律效力。

items.en: English validity is recorded with both legal and logical senses; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语里这个词的法律义与逻辑义都有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Psychology and statistics made validity a technical measure of tests in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 心理学与统计学在二十世纪把「效度」变成测验的技术指标。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like validity; the second names qualities often confused with it.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「本词」相近；第二组是常与它混淆的其他性质。

entries.definition: The adjective for something that holds legally, logically or as a measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指在法律、逻辑或测量上站得住的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb for making or proving something valid.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物生效或证明其有效的动词。

entries.definition: The act or process of validating.
entries.definitionCN: 验证或使生效的行为与过程。

entries.definition: Not valid; the negative prefix reverses the strength.
entries.definitionCN: 无效的；否定前缀把「强」反过来。

entries.definition: Prized or assessed at a price, from the same verb but another sense.
entries.definitionCN: 受重视或已估价的，同源动词的另一义。

entries.definition: Consistency of measurement; a test can be reliable without being valid.
entries.definitionCN: 测量的稳定性；一个测验可以可靠却无效度。

entries.definition: Closeness to the true value, a narrower idea than validity.
entries.definitionCN: 接近真值的程度，比效度更窄。

entries.definition: The quality of being well founded in reason or structure.
entries.definitionCN: 在理由或结构上有充分根据的性质。

entries.definition: Acceptance under law or custom, close to the legal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 在法律或惯例下被接受，接近法律义。

entries.definition: The power to produce a wanted result, which is not the same as being valid.
entries.definitionCN: 产生想要结果的能力，与「有效度」并不相同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin strength word, the real legal sense and real measurement terms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁「力量」词、真实法律义与真实测量术语。

normal.en: Validity comes from valere, to be strong: something valid is strong enough to stand.
normal.cn: validity 来自 valere「强」：有效的东西强到能站住。

normal.en: Law asks whether a document stands; logic asks whether an argument stands; measurement asks whether a test stands.
normal.cn: 法律问文件站不站住；逻辑问论证站不站住；测量问测验站不站住。

normal.en: Fixed phrases include internal validity, external validity and construct validity.
normal.cn: 固定说法有内部效度、外部效度与构念效度。

normal.en: A passport has validity, and so does a contract, and the two senses are close.
normal.cn: 护照有有效期，合同有法律效力，这两个义项彼此很近。

normal.en: Reliability is steadiness; validity is whether the steady thing is the right thing.
normal.cn: 可靠性是稳；效度是问这个稳的东西是不是对的东西。

abstract.en: Validity is the question of whether the ruler is measuring length or only casting a shadow.
abstract.cn: 效度问的是：这把尺在量长度，还是只在投下影子。

abstract.en: A strong claim needs a strong instrument behind it.
abstract.cn: 强的主张背后需要强的工具。

abstract.en: A test can be perfectly consistent and still measure the wrong thing.
abstract.cn: 一个测验可以完全一致，却仍在测错东西。

examples.en: The study's validity was weakened by the missing control group.
examples.cn: 缺少对照组削弱了这项研究的效度。

examples.en: She tested the validity of the scale against a second measure.
examples.cn: 她用另一种测量核对了这个量表的效度。

examples.en: The visa's validity ends on the last day of the month.
examples.cn: 签证的有效期在当月最后一天结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瓦立的题」——一块瓦立得住、题目站得稳：有效性

root: 这个词源自拉丁 validitas「力量、有效」，来自 validus「强壮的」，更早为 valere「有力量、有价值」，经法语 validite 进入英语。法律有效义较早，测量效度义在二十世纪心理学与统计中发展；词源清楚，最早记录年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one kind of strength: measuring the right thing, legal force, sound argument, trustworthy data, a document's period, logical form, internal validity, and external validity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一种「强」：测到该测之物、法律效力、论点站得住、数据可信、证件有效期、逻辑形式、内部效度，以及外部效度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance whose pointer rests exactly at the centre, with a stamped certificate beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平指针正停在中间，旁边压着一张盖章证书。

branches.en: THE MEASURE AND THE DESIGN: whether a test measures the right thing, and whether a study isolates the cause.
branches.cn: 测量与设计：测验是否测到对的东西，以及研究是否把原因隔开。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT AND ITS CLOCK: legal force, and the period during which that force lasts.
branches.cn: 文件与它的时钟：法律效力，以及效力持续的期限。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT: a claim that stands in substance, and a form that holds whatever the content.
branches.cn: 论证：在内容上站得住的主张，以及无论内容如何都成立的形式。

branches.en: THE DATA: evidence must stand before a conclusion may lean on it.
branches.cn: 数据：证据必须先站住，结论才能靠上去。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDE: a result strong inside the sample may still fail beyond it.
branches.cn: 外面：在样本内部很强的结果，出了样本仍可能不成立。

intro.en: Validity is a Latin abstract noun built on validus and the ending -itas, which reached English through French -ite.
intro.cn: validity 是拉丁抽象名词，建立在 validus 与后缀 -itas 上，经法语 -ite 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, validus and validitas supply the word, and the abstract ending -itas became English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 valere、validus 与 validitas 提供这个词，抽象后缀 -itas 变成英语 -ity。

items.example: The adjective supplies the family stem.

items.example: The abstract noun is the direct source.

items.example: It builds validitas and becomes English -ity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成拉丁语 validitas，并在英语里变为表示性质的后缀。

items.example: French carried the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个词带进英语。

items.example: English kept both the legal and logical senses.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了法律义与逻辑义。

items.example: It builds validity, reliability and clarity.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「效度」「可靠性」「清晰度」的三个名词。

items.example: The negative prefix reverses the quality.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀把这性质反过来。

senses.title: A disadvantage
senses.definition: a feature that makes something less good or less useful
senses.definitionCN: （名词）使某物不那么好或不那么有用的特点
senses.example: The only drawback of the flat is that it faces a busy road.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓唯一的缺点就是临着一条繁忙的路。
senses.why: A glossy photo of a new car with one rusted wheel arch showing at the corner.
senses.whyCN: 一张漂亮的新车照片，角落露出一个生锈的轮拱。

senses.title: A hindrance in a plan
senses.definition: a condition that hinders progress or success
senses.definitionCN: （名词）阻碍进展或成功的条件
senses.example: Lack of funding is a real drawback to the scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 资金不足是这个方案的真正障碍。
senses.why: One line of a plan circled in red while the rest is checked off.
senses.whyCN: 计划表上被红笔圈出的一行，其余都已打勾。

senses.title: A refund of duty
senses.definition: a refund of customs duty on imported goods that are later exported
senses.definitionCN: （名词）进口货物后来出口时退还的关税
senses.example: The exporter claimed drawback on the re-exported parts.
senses.exampleCN: 出口商为复出口的零件申请了退税。
senses.why: A customs window handing a stack of duty back across the counter.
senses.whyCN: 海关窗口把一叠税款从柜台递回。

intro.en: Drawback is draw plus back, something drawn back; it first named a drawback of duty, money drawn back from the customs, and only later a feature that pulls the value of a thing back down.
intro.cn: drawback 由 draw 加 back 组成，被拉回来的东西；它最初指关税退还，即从海关拉回来的钱，后来才指把某物价值往下拉的特点。

definition_zh: 波动；涨落；起伏
definition_en: irregular rising and falling in level, amount or condition
core_image: 一条上下起伏的曲线，像水面被风推起的波纹
scene: 这里指「波动」。 Currency fluctuation made the importer's costs change from month to month.
sceneCN: 这里 fluctuation 是「波动」（第 1 个义项：数值上下不规则变化）；句意：汇率波动让进口商的成本逐月变化。图中可辨识物件：汇率曲线、天平、货柜、日历。

pos.zh: 波动；涨落；起伏

senses.title: Prices moving up and down
senses.titleCN: 价格波动：今天高明天低
senses.definition: irregular changes in the price or value of something over time
senses.definitionCN: 某物价格或价值随时间的不规则变化
senses.example: Price fluctuation in the grain market makes planning difficult for farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 粮食市场的价格波动让农民难以规划。
senses.why: fluctus means 'wave'. Prices are pictured as a surface that rises and falls, not as a line that simply goes up.
senses.whyCN: fluctus 意为“波浪”。价格被想象成上下起伏的水面，而不是一条只往上的线。

senses.title: Physical rise and fall
senses.titleCN: 涨落：水位与波动的物理过程
senses.definition: the rising and falling of a physical quantity such as water level or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 水位、压力等物理量的上升与下降
senses.example: The fluctuation of the tide controls when the harbor can be entered.
senses.exampleCN: 潮位的涨落决定何时能进港。
senses.why: This is the literal wave sense. The noun was first used for water and air before it was used for money.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面的波浪义。这个名词先用于水与空气，之后才用于金钱。

senses.title: Statistical variation
senses.titleCN: 统计涨落：平均值附近的抖动
senses.definition: random variation around an average value in measurements or counts
senses.definitionCN: 测量或计数中围绕平均值的随机变化
senses.example: The detector's fluctuation is small enough to be averaged out.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器的涨落小到可以被平均掉。
senses.why: Statistics formalizes the wave: variation is expected, and the word names the up-and-down motion around a mean.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把波浪形式化：变化是预期之中的，这个词命名围绕均值的上下运动。

senses.title: Moods going up and down
senses.titleCN: 情绪起伏：心情像水面一样晃
senses.definition: changes in mood or emotion that go up and down without a fixed pattern
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或心情无固定规律地上下变化
senses.example: Her mood fluctuation worried the people who worked with her.
senses.exampleCN: 她的情绪起伏让共事的人担忧。
senses.why: The metaphor moves inward: feelings are treated as a liquid level that rises and falls, out of the person's control.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内部：情绪被当作会涨落的水位，不受本人控制。

senses.title: Numbers in a population
senses.titleCN: 数量起伏：人多人少来回变
senses.definition: changes in the size of a population, group or quantity over time
senses.definitionCN: 人口、群体或数量随时间的变化
senses.example: The fluctuation of the bird population follows the rainfall cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟类数量的起伏跟随降雨周期。
senses.why: Ecology counts individuals instead of dollars. The shape of the change is the same: not a trend but a repeated rise and fall.
senses.whyCN: 生态学数的是个体而非美元。变化形状相同：不是趋势，而是反复的升降。

senses.title: Quantum fluctuation
senses.titleCN: 量子涨落：真空里短暂的起伏
senses.definition: in physics, a temporary random change in the energy of a quantum system or field
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中指量子系统或场能量的短暂随机变化
senses.example: Quantum fluctuation explains why empty space is never perfectly empty.
senses.exampleCN: 量子涨落解释了为何真空从不是完美的空。
senses.why: The word reaches its most technical point here: a value that briefly departs from its expected level and returns, like a ripple in nothing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在这里达到最技术化的程度：数值短暂离开期望水平又回来，像“无”中的一圈涟漪。

senses.title: Business cycles
senses.titleCN: 经济波动：繁荣与萧条交替
senses.definition: the recurring expansion and contraction of economic activity
senses.definitionCN: 经济活动的周期性扩张与收缩
senses.example: The study links employment fluctuation to the investment cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究把就业波动与投资周期联系起来。
senses.why: Large-scale economics uses the plural almost always: fluctuations are many waves, not one. The word pictures an economy breathing in and out.
senses.whyCN: 宏观经济学几乎总用复数：波动是许多道浪，不是一道。这个词把经济画成在吸气与呼气。

senses.title: Any irregular change
senses.titleCN: 起伏不定：没有稳定的时候
senses.definition: any change that repeatedly moves away from and back toward a previous level
senses.definitionCN: 任何反复离开先前水平又返回的变化
senses.example: The fluctuation in his attendance made the coach drop him from the team.
senses.exampleCN: 他出勤的起伏让教练把他踢出了队。
senses.why: The general sense keeps the essential shape: movement that is not a steady climb or fall but an oscillation around a level.
senses.whyCN: 总义保留基本形状：不是稳定的升或降，而是围绕某个水平的摆动。

intro.en: Fluctuation comes from Latin fluctuatio, built on fluctuare 'to move in waves', from fluctus 'a wave', from fluere 'to flow'. The word has described water, then prices, then quantum fields.
intro.cn: fluctuation 来自拉丁 fluctuatio，建立在 fluctuare“波浪式运动”之上，而 fluctus“波浪”又源自 fluere“流动”。这个词先后描述水、价格与量子场。

items.en: fluere meant 'to flow'. Its present participle fluens gives English fluent, and the adjective fluidus gives fluid; the same root underlies influence and affluent with different prefixes.
items.cn: fluere 意为“流动”。其现在分词 fluens 生出英语 fluent，形容词 fluidus 生出 fluid；同一词根也见于 influence、affluent，但前缀不同。

items.en: fluctus meant 'a wave, a billow'. It is a fourth-declension noun from the same verb, naming the result of flowing.
items.cn: fluctus 意为“波浪、涌浪”。它是同一动词派生的第四变格名词，命名“流动”的结果。

items.en: fluctuare 'to wave, to move like a wave' turns the noun into a verb. The motion is not directional; it rises and falls around a level.
items.cn: fluctuare“波动、像波浪一样运动”把名词变成动词。这种运动没有固定方向，而是围绕某个水平上下。

items.en: fluctuatio names the action or state of waving. English borrows this form as fluctuation in the 17th century, first for physical motion.
items.cn: fluctuatio 命名“波动”的动作或状态。英语于 17 世纪以 fluctuation 借入这一形式，最初用于物理运动。

items.en: From the 18th and 19th centuries the word spreads to prices, markets and populations, where the up-and-down shape is statistical rather than physical.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪，这个词扩展到价格、市场与人口，其上下形状变为统计性的而非物理性的。

items.en: In the 20th century quantum physics adopts the word for short-lived random variations of a field, the smallest possible waves.
items.cn: 20 世纪量子物理采用该词，指场中短暂随机的变化，即最小的波浪。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the flu- root but splits into flow, wave and adjective forms; the near-meaning group all describe change, with different shapes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 flu- 词根，但分为流动、波浪与形容词形式；近义组都描述变化，但形状不同。

entries.definition: to rise and fall irregularly. It is the action; fluctuation is the resulting movement as a noun.
entries.definitionCN: 不规则地上下波动。它是动作；fluctuation 是作为名词的波动。

entries.definition: speaking or flowing smoothly. It comes from the present participle of fluere 'flow', so it describes smooth flow, not wave motion.
entries.definitionCN: 流利的；流畅的。它来自 fluere“流动”的现在分词，因此描述顺畅流动，而非波浪。

entries.definition: a substance that flows; also smooth or changeable. It names flow, while fluctuation names oscillation.
entries.definitionCN: 流体；流动的；易变的。它命名“流”，而 fluctuation 命名“摆”。

entries.definition: a change or difference in condition or level. It is broader and need not go up and down.
entries.definitionCN: 状态或水平的变化或差异。它更宽泛，不必上下反复。

entries.definition: regular movement back and forth. It is more regular than fluctuation, which is often irregular.
entries.definitionCN: 有规律的往返运动。它比 fluctuation 更规则，后者常不规则。

entries.definition: the quality of being likely to change or fail. It judges the change as a problem, while fluctuation merely describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 易变或易失稳的性质。它把变化判定为问题，而 fluctuation 只作描述。

entries.definition: a noticeable change from one level or opinion to another. It is informal and usually suggests a bigger range.
entries.definitionCN: 从一个水平或立场到另一个的明显变化。它口语化，通常暗示幅度更大。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fluere 'flow' gives fluctus 'wave': fluctuation is a level flowing up and down.
normal.cn: fluere“流动”生出 fluctus“波浪”：fluctuation 就是水平面上下流动。

normal.en: fluent, fluid and fluctuation share the flu- stem but split into smooth flow, substance and oscillation.
normal.cn: fluent、fluid、fluctuation 共享 flu- 词干，但分别指向顺畅流动、流体与摆动。

normal.en: price fluctuation, market fluctuation and exchange-rate fluctuation are the three everyday collocations.
normal.cn: price fluctuation、market fluctuation、exchange-rate fluctuation 是三个日常搭配。

normal.en: Quantum fluctuation is the smallest wave: a value briefly leaves its level and returns.
normal.cn: 量子涨落是最小的波浪：数值短暂离开原位又回来。

normal.en: Fluctuation is neutral, instability is negative; one describes the motion, the other judges it.
normal.cn: fluctuation 中性，instability 负面；一个描述运动，一个评判运动。

abstract.en: Think of a cork bobbing on water, rising and sinking without travelling anywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一个软木塞在水上上下浮动，却没有去往任何地方。

abstract.en: Think of a graph line that keeps crossing its own average, again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一条曲线反复穿过自己的平均值。

abstract.en: Think of a heartbeat monitor: the line is never flat, and that is what life looks like.
abstract.cn: 想象心跳监护仪：线从不平直，而生命就是这个样子。

examples.en: Small fluctuations in temperature can change the result of the experiment.
examples.cn: 温度的微小波动就能改变实验结果。

examples.en: The central bank tries to limit fluctuation in the currency.
examples.cn: 央行试图限制货币的波动。

examples.en: Seasonal fluctuation in demand is normal in the tourism industry.
examples.cn: 旅游业的季节性需求波动是正常的。

dict_mnemonic.text: “浮（flu）起来又沉下去”——水面上下浮沉，像价格线来回走 → fluctuation 波动

root: 拉丁 fluere“流动” → fluctus“波浪” → fluctuare“波动” → fluctuatio；核心是“围绕某一水平的上下起伏”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one shape: a level rises and falls around a mean, never settling and never simply climbing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一种形状：某个水平围绕均值上下，既不安定，也不是单纯上升。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a water surface pushed into ripples by wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：被风推起波纹的水面。

branches.en: MARKETS: price and business-cycle fluctuation are the same wave seen in a day and in a decade.
branches.cn: 市场：价格波动与经济周期波动，是同一种波浪在一天与十年两个尺度上的样子。

branches.en: PHYSICAL: tide and pressure fluctuation are the literal water-and-air version of the word.
branches.cn: 物理：潮位与压力涨落，是这个词字面上的水与空气版本。

branches.en: RANDOMNESS: statistical variation and quantum fluctuation are small departures from an expected level.
branches.cn: 随机性：统计涨落与量子涨落，都是对期望水平的微小偏离。

branches.en: LIVING THINGS: mood and population fluctuation move the wave from matter to feeling and to counts of organisms.
branches.cn: 生命：情绪与数量波动，把这道浪从物质移到情感与生物计数。

branches.en: GENERAL SHAPE: any repeated departure and return is the same oscillation, whatever the unit.
branches.cn: 一般形状：任何反复离开又返回的运动都是同一种摆动，不论单位是什么。

intro.en: Fluctuation is fluctuate plus -ion. The flu- stem means 'flow', -ct- marks the wave noun, -ate makes a verb and -ion names the motion.
intro.cn: fluctuation 是 fluctuate 加 -ion。flu- 词干意为“流动”，-ct- 标记波浪名词，-ate 构成动词，-ion 命名运动。

latinIntro.en: The family runs from fluere 'flow' to fluctus 'wave' to fluctuare 'wave' to fluctuatio. English relatives include fluent, fluid, influence and affluent.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族从 fluere“流动”到 fluctus“波浪”到 fluctuare“波动”再到 fluctuatio。英语同族词包括 fluent、fluid、influence、affluent。

items.meaningCN: 波动；起伏（-ate 动词后缀）
items.exampleCN: 整个夏天价格都在波动。

items.meaning: the motion of rising and falling
items.meaningCN: 波动；涨落（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The fluctuation was within five percent.
items.exampleCN: 波动幅度在百分之五以内。

items.meaningCN: 波动的（-ing 分词形容词）
items.example: The fluctuating demand strained the supply chain.
items.exampleCN: 波动的需求让供应链吃紧。

items.meaning: wavy, moving up and down, now rare
items.meaningCN: 波动的（-ant 形容词，罕用）
items.example: The fluctuant surface made landing difficult.
items.exampleCN: 起伏的水面让降落很困难。

items.meaning: relating to fluctuation, used in physics
items.meaningCN: 涨落的（-al 关系形容词，物理学用）
items.example: Fluctuational noise sets the limit of the sensor.
items.exampleCN: 涨落噪声决定了传感器的极限。

items.meaningCN: 流利的（fluere 现在分词，同一词根）
items.example: She is fluent in three languages.
items.exampleCN: 她能流利使用三种语言。

items.meaningCN: 流体；易变的（-idus 形容词）
items.example: The fluid in the pipe was replaced.
items.exampleCN: 管道里的流体被更换了。

items.meaning: a flowing-in of power or effect

items.example: The climate has a strong influence on crops.
items.exampleCN: 气候对作物有很大影响。
